docs.text:
XTS API

XTS API (Xtreme Trading System API) is a complete trading framework that connects your application directly to brokers and stock exchanges — enabling market data, order management, portfolio services, and real-time updates.

Secure authentication Place & manage orders Portfolio & holdings Real-time WebSocket Live market quotes Easy integration

docs.title: What is XTS API?
docs.text:
XTS API acts as a bridge between your application and the stock exchange. It separates into two independent channels — Market Data (read-only feeds) and Interactive (two-way trading operations) — so network traffic never interferes with your orders.

Market Data APIRead-only market information
  • Live market quotes & OHLC
  • Historical price data
  • Market depth (order book)
  • Instrument search
  • WebSocket quote streaming
Interactive APITwo-way trading operations
  • User authentication & sessions
  • Place / Modify / Cancel orders
  • Holdings & positions
  • Funds & margin
  • Real-time order updates

docs.title: About RMoney
docs.text:
RMoney is a technology-driven stock broking and investment platform that provides traders and investors with access to financial markets through modern trading applications, desktop platforms, and APIs.

RMoney enables users to trade across multiple market segments including Equity, Futures & Options (F&O), Currency, and Commodities. Along with manual trading, RMoney also provides API-based trading infrastructure that allows developers and traders to build custom applications, automate trading strategies, and access market data programmatically.

docs.title: What are RMoney APIs?
docs.text:
RMoney APIs are a collection of developer interfaces that allow applications to communicate directly with the RMoney trading ecosystem. Instead of placing orders manually, developers can use APIs to perform actions automatically.

  • Retrieve live market prices
  • Access historical market data
  • Place buy and sell orders
  • Track positions and holdings
  • Monitor portfolios
  • Receive real-time market updates
  • Build algorithmic trading systems

These APIs are based on the Symphony XTS framework and are designed for high-speed trading and market data access.

docs.text:
RMoney APIs help developers and traders build powerful financial applications without needing to create trading infrastructure from scratch.

  • Automated trading

Whether you are building a simple stock tracker or a complete algorithmic trading platform, RMoney APIs provide the building blocks required for development.

docs.title: Reference Manual
docs.text:
📘 The Complete Reference Manual: Symphony XTS API v2 & Python Client Library

Welcome! This is a comprehensive, standalone guide designed for new users and programmers to master the Symphony XTS Front-End API (v2.0) and its official Python client library, xts-api-client.

No prior experience with trading APIs is required. We explain everything from high-level architecture to low-level parameters, supplemented by visual diagrams and code examples.

docs.title: 1High-Level Concepts & Mental Models
docs.text:
What is XTS?

Symphony XTS is a high-speed trading system interface. It sits between your custom software (trading bot, dashboard, or scanner) and the stock brokers/exchanges (like NSE, BSE, MCX).

The Two-Channel Split (Dual Engine)

To prevent network traffic jams, XTS separates commands into two entirely independent channels:

  • Interactive API : Private and secure. Used to place trades, check cash balances, query open positions, and get instant notifications when your orders fill.
  • Market Data API : Public and read-only. Used to fetch stock names, request historical candle data, and stream real-time price updates (LTP, bid/ask spreads).

docs.title: 2Technical Vocabulary & Business Rules
docs.text:
Before writing code, you must understand the terminology used in API parameters:

A. Exchange Segments

Tells XTS which market segment you are querying:

  • NSECM (1): National Stock Exchange Cash Market (Buying actual shares of Reliance, TCS, etc.)
  • NSEFO (2):National Stock Exchange Futures & Options (Trading Nifty options/futures)
  • NSECD (3): National Stock Exchange Currency Derivatives (USD/INR trading)
  • MCXFO (51): Multi Commodity Exchange Futures & Options (Gold, Silver, Crude Oil)
  • BSECM (11) & BSEFO (12): Bombay Stock Exchange equivalents
B. Product Types

Tells the broker how to manage the trade margin and holding period:

  • MIS (Margin Intraday Square-off): Closed automatically before market shuts. Offers high leverage.
  • NRML (Normal): Used to hold futures & options contracts for multiple days.
  • CNC (Cash and Carry): Used to buy actual stock shares for long-term investing. No leverage.
C. Order Types
  • MARKET: Buys/sells immediately at the best available current market price.
  • LIMIT: Executes only at your specified price or better.
  • STOPMARKET: Triggered when the market price hits a target trigger price, then executes as a Market order.
  • STOPLIMIT: Triggered when the market price hits a target trigger price, then places a Limit order.
D. Time In Force (Validity)
  • DAY: The order is valid until the market closes today.
  • IOC (Immediate or Cancel): The order must execute instantly, or any unfilled part is cancelled.
  • FOK (Fill or Kill): The entire order must execute instantly in full, or the whole order is cancelled.

docs.title: 4REST API Reference: Authentication & Session
docs.text:
Every action requires a session token. Here is the lifecycle of an XTS session:

---

docs.title:
Authentication Endpoints
  • Interactive Login: POST /interactive/user/session
  • Interactive Logout: DELETE /interactive/user/session
  • Market Data Login: POST /apimarketdata/auth/login
  • Market Data Logout: DELETE /apimarketdata/auth/logout

Python Authentication Code Example 
import asyncio
from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect

async def manage_session():
    # 1. Initialize the clients
    interactive_client = XTSConnect(
        apiKey="your_interactive_key",
        secretKey="your_interactive_secret",
        source="WEBAPI",
        root="https://api.yourbroker.com"
    )

    # 2. Login (This fetches and automatically saves the token to client.token)
    login_resp = await interactive_client.interactive_login()
    print("Interactive Logged In! Token:", interactive_client.token)
    print("User ID:", interactive_client.userID)

    # 3. Log out to clean up session
    logout_resp = await interactive_client.interactive_logout()
    print("Logged out successfully!")

asyncio.run(manage_session())
5Interactive API (Trading Operations)
docs.text:
The Interactive client manages your money, orders, and positions.

A. Order Placement & The Order Lifecycle

When you submit an order, it moves through a state machine inside the exchange:

B. Order Parameters Deep Dive

When calling place_order(), you must specify the following parameters:

response = await client.place_order(
    exchangeSegment="NSECM",           # "NSECM", "NSEFO", "MCXFO"
    exchangeInstrumentID=2885,         # Numeric code for the stock (e.g. 2885 for RELIANCE)
    productType="MIS",                 # "MIS" (Intraday), "NRML" (F&O Carryover), "CNC" (Equity Delivery)
    orderType="LIMIT",                 # "MARKET", "LIMIT", "STOPMARKET", "STOPLIMIT"
    orderSide="BUY",                   # "BUY" or "SELL"
    timeInForce="DAY",                 # "DAY", "IOC"
    disclosedQuantity=0,               # Quantity visible to public order book (0 hides nothing)
    orderQuantity=10,                  # Total quantity to buy/sell
    limitPrice=2450.50,                # Price to execute (required if LIMIT or STOPLIMIT)
    stopPrice=0.0,                     # Trigger price (required if STOPMARKET or STOPLIMIT)
    orderUniqueIdentifier="my_bot_01"  # Custom string tag to track this specific order
)
C. Advanced Order Types (Cover & Bracket) 1. Cover Orders (CO)

A Cover Order has a stop-loss order chained directly to it. It is highly leveraged and requires an entry transaction and a trigger price (the stop-loss activation level).

1. Entry Order(Market or Limit) If Filled ⟶ 2. Stop Loss triggerPrice(Active on Exchange) If price hits Trigger level ⟶ 3. Executed Exit(Market Order)

Cover Order Parameters & Code:

# Place a Cover Order: Buy Reliance at market, stop-loss trigger active at ₹2400
co_response = await client.place_cover_order(
    exchangeSegment="NSECM",
    exchangeInstrumentID=2885,
    orderSide="BUY",
    orderType="MARKET",
    orderQuantity=5,
    disclosedQuantity=0,
    limitPrice=0.0,                    # 0.0 because orderType is MARKET
    stopPrice=2400.0,                  # Stop Loss Trigger level
    orderUniqueIdentifier="co_trade_01"
)
2. Bracket Orders (BO)

A Bracket Order surrounds your entry order with two bracket legs: a Take Profit Target and a Stop-Loss Protection. Both exit orders are sent to the exchange as a One-Cancels-the-Other (OCO) pair.

Bracket Order Parameters & Code:

# Place a Bracket Order: Buy Reliance at ₹2450. Sell at ₹2500 for profit (+50) or ₹2420 for loss (-30)
bo_response = await client.place_bracketorder(
    exchangeSegment="NSECM",
    exchangeInstrumentID=2885,
    orderType="LIMIT",
    orderSide="BUY",
    disclosedQuantity=0,
    orderQuantity=10,
    limitPrice=2450.00,
    squarOff=50.0,                     # Profit target offset (added to entry price)
    stopLossPrice=30.0,                # Stop-Loss protection offset (subtracted from entry price)
    trailingStoploss=0.0,              # 0.0 means inactive. Set value to adjust SL up as price rises
    isProOrder=False,                  # Set True for proprietary trading accounts
    orderUniqueIdentifier="bo_trade_01"
)
D. Spread & GTT Orders 1. Spread Orders

Spread orders let you trade price differences between two stock options or futures contracts simultaneously (e.g. buying July Futures and selling August Futures).

  • Place Spread: POST /interactive/orders/spread
  • Modify Spread: PUT /interactive/orders/spread
  • Cancel Spread: DELETE /interactive/orders/spread
2. GTT (Good-Till-Triggered) Orders

GTT orders remain active in the system for weeks or months until a target trigger price is hit. Once hit, it launches a standard order.

  • Place GTT: POST /interactive/orders/gtt
  • GTT Order Book: GET /interactive/orders/gtt/orderbook
  • Cancel GTT: DELETE /interactive/orders/gtt
E. Portfolio Management & Positions

Once you have active trades, you query your balances and positions:

async def query_portfolio(client):
    # 1. Available margin and cash balance
    balance = await client.get_balance()
    available_cash = balance['result']['BalanceList'][0]['limitObject']['RMSSubLimits']['cashAvailable']
    print(f"Available Cash: ₹{available_cash}")

    # 2. Holdings (Long-term stocks held in your demat account)
    holdings = await client.get_holding()
    print("Holdings List:", holdings['result'])

    # 3. Daywise positions (Today's trading activity)
    day_pos = await client.get_position_daywise()

    # 4. Netwise positions (Current active net open positions)
    net_pos = await client.get_position_netwise()
    for pos in net_pos['result']:
        print(f"Instrument: {pos['ExchangeInstrumentID']} | Open Qty: {pos['NetQty']} | MTM PnL: ₹{pos['MTM']}")

    # 5. Convert Position (e.g., convert Intraday 'MIS' to Delivery 'CNC')
    await client.convert_position(
        exchangeSegment="NSECM",
        exchangeInstrumentID=2885,
        targetQty=5,
        isDayWise=True,
        oldProductType="MIS",
        newProductType="CNC"
    )
F. Margin Calculator APIs

You can request how much cash margin is required to place or modify orders before actually sending them:

  • Regular Margin: POST /interactive/margin/regular
  • Cover Margin: POST /interactive/margin/cover
  • Bracket Margin: POST /interactive/margin/bracket
---

docs.title: 6Market Data API (Feeds & Queries)
docs.text:
The Market Data client fetches historical chart candles, instrument identifiers, and subscriptions.

async def query_market_data(market_client):
    # 1. Search for a security by trading symbol
    search_resp = await market_client.search_by_scriptname("TATAMOTORS")
    instrument_id = search_resp['result'][0]['ExchangeInstrumentID']
    print(f"TATA Motors Instrument ID: {instrument_id}")

    # 2. Query Expiry Dates for Options/Futures contracts
    expiries = await market_client.get_expiry_date(
        exchangeSegment=2,             # NSEFO
        series="OPTIDX",               # Index Option
        symbol="NIFTY"
    )
    print("Nifty Option Expiries:", expiries['result'])

    # 3. Retrieve Historical Chart Candles (OHLC)
    candles = await market_client.get_ohlc(
        exchangeSegment=1,             # NSECM
        exchangeInstrumentID=22,       # NIFTY Index
        startTime="Jun 01 2026 091500",  # MMM DD YYYY HHMMSS
        endTime="Jun 15 2026 153000",
        compressionValue=5             # 5-minute intervals
    )
    print("Raw Candle Data:", candles['result']['dataReponse'][:200])

docs.title: 7Real-time Socket Streaming (WebSockets via Socket.IO)
docs.text:
WebSockets establish a constant, open channel of communication. Data flows automatically without your software having to ask for it.

Step 1: Connection URL Breakdown

The library connects to the socket using a specific query string:

  • Interactive Socket: {root_url}/?token={token}&userID={userID}&apiType=INTERACTIVE
  • Market Data Socket: {root_url}/?token={token}&userID={userID}&publishFormat=JSON&broadcastMode=Full
Step 2: The Event Code Map

The Market Data socket streams message packets prefixed with numeric event codes:

Step 3: Complete WebSocket Listener Implementation

To catch these events, you subclass MarketDataSocketClient (for prices) or InteractiveSocketClient (for trading updates) and assign it to the socket managers:

import asyncio
from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect
from xts_api_client.market_data_socket import MDSocket_io
from xts_api_client.market_data_socket_client import MarketDataSocketClient

# 1. Create your listener implementation
class RealTimePriceFeed(MarketDataSocketClient):
    async def on_connect(self):
        print(" Connected to live price feeds!")

    async def on_disconnect(self):
        print(" Socket disconnected!")

    async def on_error(self, data):
        print(" Error from Socket:", data)

    # Event 1512: LTP Ticks
    async def on_event_last_traded_price_full(self, data):
        print(f"Price Tick -> ID: {data['ExchangeInstrumentID']} | Price: ₹{data['LastTradedPrice']}")

    # Event 1501: Bid/Ask Depth Ticks
    async def on_event_touchline_full(self, data):
        print(f"Spread -> Bid: {data['BidInfo']['Price']} | Ask: {data['AskInfo']['Price']}")

# 2. Main initialization script
async def stream_prices():
    # Login HTTP first
    client = XTSConnect(
        apiKey="your_market_key",
        secretKey="your_market_secret",
        source="WEBAPI",
        root="https://api.yourbroker.com"
    )
    await client.marketdata_login()

    # Assign socket listener
    listener = RealTimePriceFeed()
    socket_client = MDSocket_io(
        token=client.token,
        userID=client.userID,
        root_url=client.root,
        marketdatasocketclient=listener
    )

    # Establish connection
    await socket_client.connect()

    # Subscribe to Reliance (2885) and Nifty (22)
    instruments = [
        {"exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 2885},
        {"exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 22}
    ]
    await client.send_subscription(Instruments=instruments, xtsMessageCode=1512)

    # Keep the program running to see ticks stream
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

    # Clean up
    await socket_client.disconnect()
    await client.marketdata_logout()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(stream_prices())

docs.title: 8Mark-To-Market (MTM) PnL Calculations
docs.text:
Symphony calculates your unrealized profit or loss (PnL) in real-time. Here is how the math works:

Total PnL = Realized PnL + Unrealized PnL Realized PnL

Realized PnL is locked in when you complete a trade loop (Buy and Sell the same contract).

Realized PnL = (Sell Price − Buy Price) × Traded Quantity Unrealized PnL

Unrealized PnL fluctuates as the market price moves. It is calculated on open positions:

  • For Long Positions (Open Quantity > 0): Unrealized PnL = (Current LTP − Average Buy Price) × Open Quantity
  • For Short Positions (Open Quantity < 0): Unrealized PnL = (Average Sell Price − Current LTP) × Open Quantity (Absolute)

docs.title: 9Helper Library Utilities
docs.text:
The client library includes xts_api_client.helper.helper to parse and manage incoming data structures automatically.

1. Master List Parser (Pandas DataFrame)

Symphony sends large stock master files as pipeline-separated string streams. The helper converts them to clean Pandas dataframes:

from xts_api_client.helper.helper import cm_master_string_to_df, fo_master_string_to_df

# Assume 'raw_csv_response' is retrieved from get_master() call
df_equities = cm_master_string_to_df(raw_csv_response)
# You can now run pandas queries
print(df_equities[df_equities['Name'] == 'RELIANCE'])
2. MS-DOS Time Zone Converter

Exchange times are given as seconds elapsed since the MS-DOS Epoch (1980-01-01). The helper translates this to standard Unix nanoseconds:

from xts_api_client.helper.helper import dostime_secomds_to_unixtime

unix_nanoseconds = dostime_secomds_to_unixtime(1464972900)
print("Standard Unix timestamp:", unix_nanoseconds)
3. Account-Wide Squareoff Helper

The helper provides a routine to retrieve all your open positions and instantly exit them at market price to protect capital in emergencies:

from xts_api_client.helper.helper import async_squareoff_all_positions_

# Retrieve all positions and close them out
sq_off_ids = await async_squareoff_all_positions_(interactive_client)
print("Emergency Squared off Order IDs:", sq_off_ids)

docs.title: 10Robust Code Design: Reconnections & Retries
docs.text:
To deploy algorithms safely, you must handle network disconnects or API timeouts. Here is a production-grade template for a Gateway wrapper that you can copy to build your systems:

import asyncio
import logging
from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect
from xts_api_client.interactive_socket import OrderSocket_io
from xts_api_client.interactive_socket_client import InteractiveSocketClient
from httpx import PoolTimeout, ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout

class OrderCallbackHandler(InteractiveSocketClient):
    def __init__(self, gateway):
        self.gateway = gateway

    async def on_connect(self):
        self.gateway.connected = True
        logging.info("WebSocket connected!")

    async def on_disconnect(self):
        self.gateway.connected = False
        logging.warning("WebSocket lost! Reconnecting...")
        asyncio.create_task(self.gateway.reconnect())

class XTSGateway:
    def __init__(self, api_url, key, secret):
        self.api_url = api_url
        self.key = key
        self.secret = secret
        self.client = None
        self.socket = None
        self.connected = False

    async def connect(self):
        # 1. Login REST API
        self.client = XTSConnect(self.key, self.secret, "WEBAPI", self.api_url)
        await self.client.interactive_login()

        # 2. Start WebSocket Connection
        self.socket = OrderSocket_io(
            token=self.client.token,
            userID=self.client.userID,
            root_url=self.client.root,
            reconnection=True,
            interactiveSocketClient=OrderCallbackHandler(self)
        )
        await self.socket.connect()

    async def place_order_safe(self, params: dict, retries=4):
        """Places orders with auto-retry on HTTP timeouts"""
        for attempt in range(retries):
            try:
                response = await self.client.place_order(**params)
                return response
            except (PoolTimeout, ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout) as timeout_exc:
                logging.warning(f"Timeout on attempt {attempt+1}/{retries}. Retrying...")
                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        raise RuntimeError("Failed to place order: Connection Timed Out")

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is the process of verifying who is making an API request before granting access to trading data and operations. Think of it like entering a secured building.

Building = RMoney API Security Guard = Authentication System ID Card = API Key / Access Token

docs.title: Why Authentication is Required
docs.text: Protect user accounts from unauthorized use Prevent unauthorized access to trading APIs Secure all trading and order operations Keep financial data private and safe Track and audit API usage per application

docs.title: Authentication Components
docs.text:
API Key

Identifies your application to the RMoney server.

RMY_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
  • Identifies the application
  • Tracks API usage per app
  • Blocks unauthorized applications
API Secret

Private key paired with your API Key for verification.

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx Never expose in frontend code. Store only in backend environment variables. Access Token

Proves the logged-in user's identity on every request.

eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...
  • Authenticates each API request
  • Grants access to user resources
  • Expires after 24 hours

docs.title: Authentication Flow
docs.text:
Step-by-step process

1Register your application on the portal 2Get your API Key and API Secret 3Call the Login API with credentials 4Receive an Access Token in the response 5Send the token in every API request header 6Access API resources — place orders, fetch data

Token validation inside the server

Request Received Extract Token from Header Verify Token Signature Check Token Expiry Validate User Identity Allow Request to Proceed

docs.title: Login Request and Response
Using the Token
docs.text:
Include the token in the Authorization header of every protected API call. No Bearer prefix is needed — send the raw token value.

GET /interactive/portfolio/holdings

Authorization: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...


GET /interactive/orders

Authorization: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...

docs.title: Authentication Errors
docs.text: Invalid Token { "error": "Invalid Token" } The token value is incorrect or malformed. Expired Token { "error": "Token Expired" } Token is valid but past its 24-hour lifetime. Refresh it. Unauthorized { "error": "Unauthorized" } No token was provided in the Authorization header.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
Keep Secrets Secure

Store API secrets only in backend environment variables. Never commit them to code repositories or expose them in frontend apps.

Always Use HTTPS

All API calls must use https://. Plain HTTP exposes your token to network interception and man-in-the-middle attacks.

Rotate Tokens Regularly

Do not use the same token indefinitely. Refresh access tokens before they expire and immediately revoke compromised tokens.

Validate Before Requesting

Always check if your token is still valid before making an API call. Re-authenticate proactively instead of handling 401 errors reactively.

docs.title: Bracket Orders
docs.text:
A Bracket Order (BO) combines three linked orders — Entry, Target, and Stop-Loss — into a single trade. Once the entry executes, the system automatically manages your exit for both profit and risk.

Auto entry & exit Risk management Auto profit booking Stop-loss protection No constant monitoring Intraday leverage

docs.title: Components of a Bracket Order
docs.text:
1. Entry Order

The first order used to enter the trade.

Buy RELIANCE at ₹2,850 2. Target Order

Profit booking — closes position when target price is reached.

Target Price = ₹2,900 3. Stop-Loss Order

Protective order — limits losses if market moves against the trade.

Stop Loss = ₹2,830

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: Place Bracket Order → Entry Executed → Target & SL Created → Exit Triggered → Other Order Cancelled

docs.title: Example — RELIANCE 100 Shares
docs.text:
Order Price Entry Price₹2,850 Target Price₹2,900 Stop-Loss Price₹2,830 Scenario 1 — Profit
  • Buy at ₹2,850
  • Price rises to ₹2,900
  • Target order executed
  • Profit booked automatically
  • Stop-loss order cancelled
Scenario 2 — Loss Limited
  • Buy at ₹2,850
  • Price falls to ₹2,830
  • Stop-loss order executed
  • Position closed automatically
  • Target order cancelled

docs.title: Bracket Order vs Cover Order
docs.text:
COVER ORDER
  • Entry + Stop-Loss only
  • No profit target
  • Only risk protection
  • Best for mandatory stop-loss traders
→ BRACKET ORDER
  • Entry + Target + Stop-Loss
  • Auto profit booking at target
  • Both profit & risk protection
  • Best for predefined target & SL traders

docs.title: Advantages & Limitations
docs.text:
Advantages
  • Automatic profit booking
  • Automatic stop-loss protection
  • Better risk management
  • No constant market monitoring
  • All related orders placed together
  • Higher intraday leverage available
Limitations
  • Mostly for intraday trading only
  • Entry, target & SL are linked
  • One exit cancels the other automatically
  • Not supported on all instruments
  • Exit depends on market conditions

docs.title: Common Use Cases!!! tip
docs.text:
📈 Intraday Trading

Open and close positions within the same trading day with automatic exits.

🛡️ Risk Management

Automatically limit losses using a predefined stop-loss.

💰 Profit Booking

Close the trade automatically when the target price is reached.

🤖 Automated Trading

Manage positions without continuously watching the market.

Always set realistic target and stop-loss prices. Ensure sufficient margin before placing a Bracket Order, and verify the entry price before submitting.

docs.title: Cover Orders
docs.text:
A Cover Order (CO) is a special order that combines a main order with a compulsory stop-loss — giving you built-in risk protection and higher leverage in a single placement.

Built-in stop-loss Higher leverage Automatic risk management Intraday trading Reduced monitoring Faster execution

docs.title: What is a Cover Order?
docs.text:
A Cover Order lets you enter a trade with a mandatory stop-loss baked in. Because the broker knows your maximum possible loss upfront, they offer higher leverage — making CO ideal for active intraday traders who want capital efficiency without manual exit monitoring.

Main Order
  • Buys or sells the stock
  • Executed immediately at market
  • Entry price defined here
Stop-Loss Order
  • Placed automatically alongside
  • Triggers if price moves against you
  • Exits position to cap the loss

docs.title: How It Works — Example
docs.text: RELIANCE — BUY Cover Order ORDER DETAILS Buy Price₹2,850 Stop Loss₹2,830 Quantity100 shares Max Risk₹20 × 100 = ₹2,000 OUTCOMES Price rises → ₹2,900Profit = ₹50 × 100 = ₹5,000 Price drops → ₹2,830SL triggered — Loss capped at ₹2,000

docs.title: Cover Order Workflow
docs.text: User Places Order → Main Order Executed → Stop-Loss Created → Market Moves → Profit or SL Triggered → Position Closed

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Mandatory Stop Loss

Every CO must have a stop-loss. It cannot be placed without one.

Higher Margin Benefit

Because risk is predefined, brokers offer more leverage for Cover Orders.

Automatic Risk Management

Stop-loss triggers automatically — no need to manually watch the market.

Intraday Only

Cover Orders are squared off automatically before market close.

Faster Execution

Predefined risk parameters allow the system to execute orders more efficiently.

docs.title: Advantages vs Limitations
docs.text:
Advantages
  • Reduced risk with automatic protection
  • Higher leverage from broker
  • Better capital utilisation
  • No manual exit needed for losses
  • Suitable for active traders
Limitations
  • Stop-loss is mandatory — cannot skip
  • Available for intraday trading only
  • Main order and SL are linked
  • SL rejection may force broker square-off
  • Not supported on all instruments

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text: Use Case Description Intraday Trading Open and close positions within the same day with protection Risk Management Prevent large losses using automatic stop-loss Leveraged Trading Trade larger positions with lower margin requirement Volatile Markets Protect positions during sudden or sharp price movements

docs.title: Exchange Messages
docs.text:
Exchange Messages are official notifications sent by the stock exchange (such as NSE or BSE) to inform traders and brokers about important market events, trading updates, or system announcements.

Official Notifications Real-time Alerts NSE & BSE Market Transparency

docs.title: What are Exchange Messages?
docs.text: Exchange Messages are official announcements from the exchange that provide important information related to trading, market operations, and system updates. They help users stay informed about anything that may affect trading activities.  OFFICIAL SOURCE Directly from NSE, BSE, or other exchanges REAL-TIME Delivered instantly when the exchange publishes them ACTIONABLE Help traders make informed decisions instantly

docs.title: Why are Exchange Messages Important?
docs.text: Stay informed about market changes as they happen Know if trading is suspended or resumed for a stock Be aware of special trading sessions or extended hours Receive important operational updates from the exchange Avoid trading issues caused by exchange announcements Improve overall market transparency and trader confidence

docs.title: Common Types of Exchange Messages
docs.text:
1. Trading Halt

The exchange temporarily stops trading for a particular stock or the entire market.

NSE Notice: Trading in ABC Ltd. has been suspended until further notice. 2. Trading Resume

The exchange announces that trading has started again after a halt.

Trading in ABC Ltd. has resumed from 11:30 AM. 3. Market Holiday Notice

The exchange informs participants about upcoming market holidays.

The stock market will remain closed on 15th August due to Independence Day. 4. Corporate Action

Information about company events — dividend, bonus shares, stock split, rights issue, merger.

XYZ Ltd. has announced a 1:1 Bonus Issue. 5. Auction Notification

The exchange announces auction sessions for unsettled trades.

Auction session will begin at 2:00 PM. 6. System Maintenance

The exchange notifies users about planned maintenance windows.

Exchange systems will undergo maintenance from 6 PM to 8 PM. 7. Price Band Revision

The exchange changes the upper or lower trading limits for a security.

The price band for ABC Ltd. has been revised from 10% to 20%. 8. Market-Wide Circuit Breaker

The exchange pauses all trading due to significant index movements.

Trading halted for 45 minutes due to a market-wide circuit breaker.

docs.title: Exchange Message Flow
docs.text: Exchange (NSE / BSE) ▼ Generates Official Announcement ▼ Broker / API Receives Message ▼ Trading Platform Displays Message ▼ Trader Reads the Notification

docs.title: Where Are Exchange Messages Displayed?
docs.text: Notifications panel     Exchange Messages section     Trading terminal     Broker dashboard     Mobile trading app

docs.title: Real-Life Example
docs.text:
You are planning to buy shares of ABC Ltd. Before placing your order, you receive this exchange message:

⚠ NSE Alert: Trading in ABC Ltd. has been suspended due to a pending corporate announcement. Since trading is temporarily halted, you cannot place or execute orders for that stock until the exchange resumes trading. The exchange message helps you avoid a failed order attempt and plan accordingly.

docs.title: Exchange Messages in Market Data API
docs.text:
The Exchange Messages endpoint allows applications to retrieve official messages published by the exchange and display them directly to traders.

Message Type Description Trading Halt Trading suspension notices for stocks or markets Trading Resume Trading restart announcements after a halt Market Holiday Exchange holiday notifications and closure dates Corporate Actions Dividend, bonus, stock split, rights issue, etc. Auction Notices Auction session timings and information System Maintenance Exchange maintenance windows and downtime Price Band Updates Changes in circuit limits or price bands General Announcements Other important exchange notifications

In Simple Words: Exchange Messages are official announcements from the stock exchange that inform traders about important market events such as trading halts, market holidays, corporate actions, auctions, and system updates. They help traders stay informed and make better trading decisions.

docs.title: Exchange Status
docs.text:
Exchange Status shows the current operating state of a stock exchange — whether it is open, closed, halted, or in a special trading session. It helps traders know if trading is currently allowed and what phase the market is in.

Market Hours Live Status NSE, BSE & MCX Session Awareness

docs.title: What is Exchange Status?
docs.text: Exchange Status indicates whether a stock exchange is currently open, closed, or in a specific trading phase. Before placing any order, traders use this to confirm that trading is available and to understand which market session is currently active.  MARKET PHASE Know which trading session is currently active ORDER SAFETY Avoid placing orders when trading is unavailable INTERRUPTIONS Stay informed about halts and special sessions

docs.title: Common Exchange Status Types
docs.text:
1. Open

The exchange is open and trading is taking place normally.

Exchange Status: OPEN Buy shares Sell shares Modify orders Cancel orders 2. Closed

The exchange is not accepting trades — market has closed or it is a holiday.

Exchange Status: CLOSED

No trading is possible until the next trading session.

3. Pre-Open

A session before regular market hours where orders can be placed but continuous trading has not started yet.

Exchange Status: PRE-OPEN

Orders can be entered/modified/cancelled. The exchange determines the opening price.

4. Post-Close

A session after regular market hours where certain activities may still be allowed.

Exchange Status: POST-CLOSE

Depending on exchange rules, some order-related activities may still be available.

5. Trading Halt

Trading has been temporarily suspended. Reasons may include:

Corporate announcements Technical issues Regulatory actions Circuit breakers Exchange Status: HALTED 6. Auction Session

A special session used for auction-related trading, such as settling short deliveries.

Exchange Status: AUCTION

Only auction-related trades are processed during this session.

7. Suspended

Trading for a specific security has been suspended until further notice. No orders can be executed for that security until the exchange lifts the suspension.

Exchange Status: SUSPENDED

docs.title: Exchange Status Lifecycle
docs.text: Market Closed ▼ Pre-Open Session ▼ Market Open ▼ (Optional) Trading Halt ▼ Trading Resumes ▼ Market Close ▼ Post-Close Session

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
10:30 AM — Market Open Exchange: NSE Status : OPEN Session : Regular Trading

You can place, modify, and cancel orders normally.

3:30 PM — Market Closed Exchange: NSE Status : CLOSED

Market has closed. New trades cannot be executed.

docs.title: Information Returned by Exchange Status API
docs.text: Field Description ExchangeName of the exchange (NSE, BSE, MCX, etc.) StatusCurrent market status — Open, Closed, Halted, Auction, etc. SessionCurrent trading session — Pre-Open, Regular, Auction, Post-Close Start TimeSession start time End TimeSession end time Last UpdatedTime when the status was last refreshed

docs.title: Why Trading Applications Use Exchange Status
docs.text: Enable or disable trading buttons based on market status Display market availability clearly to the user Prevent invalid order placement outside trading hours Inform users about market sessions and transitions Synchronize application behaviour with the exchange

docs.title: Real-Life Example
docs.text:
You open a trading app at 8:45 AM.

8:45 AM Exchange: NSE Status : PRE-OPEN

You can place orders, but regular trading hasn't started yet.

9:15 AM Exchange: NSE Status : OPEN

Regular trading has begun. Orders can now be matched and executed.

In Simple Words: Exchange Status tells you the current state of the stock exchange — such as Open, Closed, Pre-Open, Halted, or Auction — so you know whether trading is available and which market session is currently active.

docs.title: Enums with Numeric Constants
docs.text:
Enums (Enumerations) are predefined sets of values used by the API to represent options, states, or configurations — using compact numeric codes for speed, consistency, and reduced payload.

Faster processing Standardized values Reduced payload Prevents invalid values Less coding errors Easier validation

docs.title: What are Enums?
docs.text:
Instead of sending long descriptive text, APIs use short codes internally. For example:

WITHOUT ENUMS "productType": "Margin Intraday Square Off" → WITH ENUMS "productType": 1 where 1 = MIS

docs.title: How Enums Work Internally
docs.text: Send productType: 1 → API maps 1 = MIS → Broker processes intraday order → Response returned

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Use enum names instead of hardcoding numbers

# Avoid
productType = 1

# Prefer
productType = ProductType.MIS

Validate values before sending

✔  BUY
✔  SELL
✖  PURCHASE   ← not a valid enum value

docs.title: 1. Exchange Segments
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description NSECM 1            - NSE(National Stock Exchange)Cash Market           - It is a normal buying/selling cash market in NSE.           - Most of the traders trade here on thr regular basis.          NSEFO 2          - NSE Futures & Options         - Derivatives segment of NSE where equity futures, index futures,           and options contracts are traded.         - It is a market of future & options trading in NSE.          NSECD 3          - NSE Currency          - Currency trading segment at NSE for exchange-traded currency           futures and options (USD/INR, EUR/INR, etc.)         - It is a market of currency trading in NSE.          BSECM 11          - BSE(Bombay Stock Exchange)Cash Market         - Cash/equity segment of BSE, the oldest stock exchange in Asia,           where stocks are bought and sold.         - It is a normal buying/selling trades market in BSE.          BSEFO 12          - BSE Futures & Options         - Derivatives segment of BSE offering equity derivatives, index           derivatives, and stock futures/options.         - It is a Future & Options trade market in BSE          BSECD 13          - BSE Currency Derivative         - Currency derivatives platform of BSE that allows trading in           exchange-listed currency futures and options.         - It is a Currency trade market in BSE.          MCXFO 51          - MCX(Multi Commodity Exchange)Future & Option         - Derivatives trading segment of MCX for commodities such as gold,           silver, crude oil, natural gas, and agricultural products.         - It is a Commodity(e.g. Physical Goods/Products) trade market          NCDEX 21          - National Commodity And Derivatives Exchange.         - A leading exchange focused on agricultural commodity futures like           soybean, chana, guar, and other agri-products.         - It is a Agriculture Commodity Exchange market

docs.title: 2. ProductType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description MIS 1          - Margin Intraday Square-off         - Intraday trading product type where positions must be squared off before market close. Provides higher leverage compared to delivery.         - MIS is used for same-day trading only called Intraday Trading.         - All trades must be closed before the market closes (9:15 AM – 3:30 PM).         - The broker gives extra money (leverage), so you can trade with a larger amount.         - If you don't close the trade, the broker will automatically close it before market close.         - After closing the trade, the broker takes back its money, and you keep your money along with any profit (or bear any loss).          NRML 2          - Normal         - Standard product type used for carrying forward positions overnight in derivatives or cash without compulsory intraday square-off.         - NRML is used to keep trades overnight or for multiple days.         - You do not need to close the trade on the same day.         - It is mainly used for Futures and Options (F&O) trading.         - You can hold the trade until the contract expiry date; after expiry, the position expires or is settled automatically.         - Brokers also provide leverage in NRML, but it is usually lower than the leverage available in MIS.          CNC 4          - Cash And Carry          - Delivery-based product type for equity trades. Shares are delivered to the Demat account, with no leverage.         - CNC is used for real stock delivery and long-term investing.         - Trades are done using your own money, with little or no leverage.         - It is mainly used for buying and selling shares (equity).         - There is no need to close the position on the same day.         - You can hold the shares for as long as you want, such as days, months, or even years.          CO 8          - Cover Order         - CO is mainly used for intraday (same-day) trading.         - Intraday order type where a market or limit order is placed along with a mandatory stop-loss order. Provides higher leverage while controlling risk.         - It focuses on safety and risk control.         - A stop-loss (loss limit) order is compulsory with every trade.         - Brokers usually provide higher leverage because the risk is controlled.         - If the market moves against you and reaches the stop-loss price, the trade is automatically exited to limit the loss.          BO 16 - Bracket Order - Advanced order type where a main order is placed with both a target (profit booking) and stop-loss. Once one is executed, the other is automatically cancelled. Can also include a trailing stop-loss. - BO focuses on both profit target and stop-loss. - It is used to balance profit and loss automatically. - It contains three orders: Entry Order, Target Profit Order, and Stop-Loss Order. - When the market reaches either the target price or the stop-loss price, the trade exits automatically. - It is mainly used for intraday trading and helps traders manage risk and profit together. MTF 32          - Margin Trading Faciity - Allows investors to buy stocks by partly paying upfront and borrowing the balance from the broker. Shares can be carried forward as long as margin requirements are met.         - MTF is used for buying shares with the help of money borrowed from the broker.         - The broker charges interest on the borrowed amount.         - You can hold the shares for as long as you want, such as days, months, or even years.         - The borrowed amount remains with the broker, and interest is charged until it is repaid.         - It allows you to buy more shares than you could using only your own money.

docs.title: 3. OrderType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Market 1          - Market Order         - An order to buy or sell immediately at the best available price in the market.         - A Market Order is executed immediately at the current market price.         - You only specify the quantity to buy or sell; the price is decided by the market.         - It is used when quick execution is more important than getting a specific price.         - Example: If TCS is trading around ₹3500 and you place a Market Buy Order, it will be executed immediately at the best available market price.          Limit 2          -  Limit Order          - An order to buy or sell at a specified price (or better).         - In a Limit Order, you set the price at which you want to buy or sell.         - The trade is executed only if the market reaches your specified price or a better price.         - It is used when getting a specific price is more important than immediate execution. - Example: If the current TCS price is ₹3500 and you place a Buy Limit Order at ₹3480, the order will execute only if TCS falls to ₹3480 or below; otherwise, it will remain pending.          StopMarket 4          - StopMarket Order         - An order that becomes a market order once a specified trigger price is reached. Used mainly to limit losses.         - In a Stop Market Order, you set a trigger price (stop price).         - When the market reaches the trigger price, the order becomes a Market Order and is executed immediately at the best available price.         - It is mainly used to limit losses or protect profits automatically. - Example: If you bought TCS at ₹3500 and set a Stop Market Sell Order with a trigger price of ₹3480, then when TCS falls to ₹3480, the order is activated and the shares are sold immediately at the current market price.          StopLimit 8          - StopLimit Order         - An order that becomes a limit order once the trigger price is reached. It executes only at the specified limit price or better.         - In a Stop Limit Order, you set both a trigger price and a limit price.         - When the market reaches the trigger price, a Limit Order is placed at the specified limit price.         - It is used to control the execution price while limiting losses or protecting profits. - Example: If you bought TCS at ₹3500, you can set a trigger price of ₹3480 and a limit price of ₹3475. When TCS reaches ₹3480, a sell order at ₹3475 is placed. The trade will execute only at ₹3475 or a better price.          OCO 32          - One Cancels the Other         - A conditional order where two linked orders are placed — if one gets executed, the other is automatically cancelled.         - OCO contains two orders together, usually a Target Order and a Stop-Loss Order.         - It helps you manage both profit and loss automatically.         - When one order is executed, the other order is automatically cancelled.         - It is useful when you want to set both a profit target and a loss limit without monitoring the market continuously.          MTF 32          - Margin Trading Facility         - MTF allows you to buy shares using money borrowed from the broker.         - You can hold the shares for a long time (days, months, or years); there is no need to close the trade on the same day          - The broker charges interest on the borrowed amount until it is repaid.         - It helps you buy more shares than you could with only your own money.

docs.title: 4. OrderSide
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description BUY 49              - BUY means purchasing a stock or contract.             - Indicates a purchase transaction. Used when entering a long position (expecting the price to rise).             - You buy when you expect the price to go up.             - Profit is made if you sell later at a higher price.              SELL 50              - SELL means selling a stock or contract.             - Indicates a sale transaction. Used when exiting a long position or initiating a short position (expecting the price to fall).             - You sell when you expect the price to go down or when you want to book profit.             - Profit is made if you buy back later at a lower price (short selling) or if you sell shares you already own at a higher price.

docs.title: 5. TimeInForce
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description DAY 1              - Day Order             - The order remains active only for the current trading day.             - If the order is not executed by market close, it is automatically cancelled.             - Order remains valid only for the trading day. If not executed by market close, it is cancelled automatically.              GTC 2              - Good Till Cancelled             - The order remains active until you cancel it manually.             - It can stay active for many days if it is not executed.             - The order is cancelled only when you manually cancel it.              IOC 4              - Immediate Or Cancel             - The order must be executed immediately.             - If only some quantity can be executed, the remaining quantity is cancelled instantly.             - Any unfilled part of the order does not stay pending.             - Example: If you place an IOC order to buy 100 shares and only 60 shares are available, those 60 shares are bought immediately and the remaining 40 shares are cancelled.              GTD 8              - Good Till Date              - The order remains active until a specific date set by you.             - It can stay active for many days until that date.             - If the order is not executed by the specified date, it is automatically cancelled.              EOS 16              - End Of Session             - The order remains active only until the end of the current trading session (market day).             - The order must be executed before the session ends.             - If the order is not executed by the end of the session, it is automatically cancelled. COL 32              - Close of Trading Session                    - COL means the order is intended to be executed near the market closing time.             - It helps traders place orders based on the closing price of the trading session.             - The order is processed during the market closing period.              GTDYS 128              - Good Till Defined Yielding Sessions              - The order remains active for a predefined number of trading sessions.             - It stays active across multiple market days until the defined session limit is reached.             - If the order is not executed within those sessions, it is automatically cancelled.

docs.title: 6. Order Status
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Open or New 48              - Open/New means a new order has been placed and is waiting to be executed.             - The order is active in the market but has not been fully or partially traded yet.             - The order can later be executed, modified, or cancelled.              PartiallyFilled 49              - PartiallyFilled Order             - It means only some part of the order has been executed.The remaining quantity is still active and waiting to be executed.             - The order stays open until the remaining quantity is filled or cancelled.              Filled 50              - Filled Order             - Filled means the order has been completely executed.             - All the requested quantity has been bought or sold successfully.              Cancelled 52              - Cancelled Order             - Cancelled means the order has been cancelled and will not be executed.             - The order may be cancelled by you, the broker, or the exchange.             - No quantity will be traded after the order is cancelled.              Replaced 53              - Replaced Order             - Replaced means an existing order has been modified or updated.             - The old order is replaced with a new one having the updated details.Changes may include price, quantity, or other order parameters.              PendingCancel 54              - PendingCancel Order             - PendingCancel means a cancellation request has been sent, but the order has not been cancelled yet.             - The system or exchange is processing the cancellation request.The order status will change to Cancelled once the cancellation is completed.          Rejected 56              - Rejected Order             - Rejected means the order was not accepted by the exchange or broker.             - The order is not executed and becomes inactive.             - Common reasons include insufficient funds, invalid price, or trading restrictions.              PendingNew 65              - PendingNew Order             - PendingNew means the order has been received but has not yet become active in the market.             - The exchange or broker is still processing the order.Once processing is complete, the status changes to Open/New.              PendingReplace 69              - PendingReplace Order             - PendingReplace means a request to modify an existing order has been sent, but the changes have not been applied yet.             - The exchange or broker is still processing the modification request.             - Once the modification is completed, the order status changes to Replaced.

docs.title: 7. Order Source
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description TWS 1              - Trader Workstation             - TWS refers to a trading terminal or trading platform used to place and manage orders.             - It provides access to market data and trading features.             - Traders can buy, sell, modify, and monitor orders through TWS.             - Example: A trader using a desktop trading application to place an order for 100 TCS shares is using a TWS (Trader Workstation).              TWSAPI 2              - Trader Workstation API             - TWSAPI means orders are placed programmatically through an API instead of manually.             - It allows applications or trading algorithms to connect directly to the trading platform.             - Orders can be placed, modified, and monitored automatically using code.             - Example: A Python program that automatically buys 100 TCS shares through the broker's API is using TWSAPI.              WEB 21              - WEB means the order was placed through a web-based trading platform or website.             - Orders entered manually by the trader through the broker's web-based trading platform.             - It indicates that the source of the order is the broker's web application.             - Traders can place, modify, and monitor orders using a browser.             - Example: If you log in to your broker's website and buy 100 TCS shares, the order source will be WEB.              WEBAPI 22              - WEBAPI means the order was placed through a web-based API, not manually through the website.             - It allows applications or programs to place and manage orders automatically.             - It allows applications or programs to place and manage orders automatically.             - Example: A Python script using a broker's REST API to buy 100 TCS shares is using WEBAPI.              MOBILEANDROID 41              - MOBILEANDROID means the order was placed using the broker's Android mobile app.             - It indicates that the source of the order is an Android device.             - Traders can place, modify, and track orders through the mobile app.             - Example: If you use your Android phone to buy 100 TCS shares through the broker's app, the order source will be MOBILEANDROID.              MOBILEIOS 81              - MOBILEIOS means the order was placed using the broker's iPhone or iPad app.             - It indicates that the source of the order is an iOS device.             - Traders can place, modify, and track orders through the mobile app.             - Example: If you use your iPhone to buy 100 TCS shares through the broker's app, the order source will be MOBILEIOS.              EnterpriseWeb 154              - EnterpriseWeb means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional web platform.             - It is typically used by organizations, brokers, or large clients rather than individual retail traders.             - Orders can be placed and managed through a specialized web-based interface.             - Example: If a mutual fund or a corporate client places an order through the broker's enterprise web portal, the order source will be EnterpriseWeb.              EnterpriseMobile 155              - EnterpriseMobile means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional mobile application.             - It is mainly used by organizations, brokers, or large clients, not regular retail traders.             - Orders can be placed and managed through a specialized mobile platform.             - Example: If a mutual fund manager places an order using the broker's enterprise mobile app, the order source will be EnterpriseMobile.              EnterpriseTWS 156              - EnterpriseTWS means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional trading workstation (TWS).             - It is mainly used by organizations, brokers, or large clients rather than individual retail traders.             - Orders can be placed, modified, and monitored through a professional trading terminal.             - Example: If a mutual fund or a brokerage firm places an order using its enterprise trading workstation, the order source will be EnterpriseTWS.

docs.title: 8. Position Square Off Mode
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description DayWise 1              - DayWise means positions or statistics are calculated separately for each trading day.             - Only the trades done on the current day are considered.             - At the end of the day, the values are reset for the next trading day.             - Example: If you buy and sell 100 TCS shares today, the profit/loss will be shown only for today's trades under DayWise.**              NetWise 2              - NetWise means all trades are combined together to show the overall (net) position.             - It considers both previous and current trades instead of only today's trades.             - It shows your total quantity, average price, and overall profit/loss.             - Example: If you bought 100 TCS shares yesterday and 50 more today, NetWise will show a total position of 150 shares.**

docs.title: 9. Position Square Off Quantity Type
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Percentage 0              - Percentage means values are shown in percentage (%) instead of actual numbers.             - It helps compare profit, loss, growth, or performance easily.             - The result is displayed as a percentage of the total value. ExactQty 1              - ExactQty means the exact quantity requested must be executed.             - The order will not be partially filled.             - If the full quantity is not available, the order may remain pending or fail based on the order rules.

docs.title: 10. MarketType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Normal 1              - Normal means regular trading.             - It is the standard order type used for normal buy and sell transactions.             - No special conditions or restrictions are applied to the order.              Oddlot 2              - It means the order is an odd lot type             - It is used when quantity is less than the standard trading lot size             - These are small or non-standard share quantities (not full lots)             - It is treated separately from normal lot trading in the system.Useful for small quantity or partial share trading orders             - Example:                 • Suppose the normal trading lot size is 100 shares                 • A trader places an order for 25 shares of Reliance Industries                 • Since 25 is less than the standard lot size (100), it is treated as an Odd Lot order                 • In the system/API, this order will be marked as: Oddlot = 2              RetailDebt 3              - represents a retail debt order type             - It is used for buying/selling debt instruments like bonds or government securities             - These trades are done by retail (individual) investors, not big institutions             - It usually involves small investment amounts              Auction 4              - represents orders placed in an auction market             - It is used when securities are traded through a bidding process instead of normal trading             - Buyers and sellers submit bids, and the best price gets matched             - It is often used in special cases like exchange auctions or settlement auctions              CallAuction1 5              - represents a specific call auction order type (Phase 1)             - Used to find a single fair market price by matching many buy and sell orders at once.             - Orders are first collected, then the system calculates one price, and finally trades are executed together in one batch.              CallAuction2 6              - means a second type of call auction session where orders are not executed instantly.             - Orders are first collected and then a single fair price is discovered by the system.             - After price discovery, all matching buy and sell orders are executed together in one batch.             - it is a batch trading mode where trades happen together at one final auction price.

docs.title: 11. OrderLegStatus
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description SingleOrderLeg 1        - means the order contains only one trading instruction (one leg).       - It is a regular standalone order, not part of a multi-leg strategy.       - The order is executed independently without being linked to other orders.       - In simple words: one order = one action (buy or sell) on a single instrument. SpreadFirstLeg 2         - means this order is the first leg of a spread strategy.        - A spread strategy consists of two or more linked orders executed together.        - The first leg is the initial buy or sell order in the spread.        - Example: Buy NIFTY July Futures (first leg) and Sell NIFTY August Futures (second leg).        SpreadSecondLeg 3        - means this order is the second leg of a spread strategy.       - It is linked to the first leg and forms part of a multi-leg trade.       - Both legs work together to implement a spread trading strategy. MultilegFirstLeg 4        - means this order is the first leg of a multi-leg trading strategy.       - A multi-leg strategy contains two or more linked orders that work together.       - This is the starting order of the strategy, followed by additional legs.       - Example: Buy a Call Option as the first leg of an options strategy.        MultilegSecondLeg 5        - means this order is the second leg of a multi-leg trading strategy.       - It is linked to the first leg and helps complete the overall strategy.       - Multiple legs are used together to achieve a specific trading objective. docs.title: GTT Orders
docs.text:
GTT (Good Till Triggered) Orders

A GTT Order stays saved with the broker until the market reaches a predefined trigger price. Once triggered, the order is automatically sent to the exchange — no need to monitor the market continuously.

Auto trigger No monitoring needed Planned trading Price-based entry Buy & sell support Long-term investing

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: Create GTT Order → Order Saved by Broker → Market Monitored → Trigger Hit → Order Executed

docs.title: Components of a GTT Order
docs.text:
Trading Symbol

The stock or instrument to trade.

RELIANCE, TCS, INFY Trigger Price

Market price that activates the GTT order.

₹2,750 → order fires Order Price

The actual price placed at exchange after trigger.

Limit ₹2,748 Quantity

Number of shares or contracts.

100 Shares

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Example 1 — Buy GTT
  • Current price: ₹2,700
  • Trigger price set: ₹2,750
  • RELIANCE rises to ₹2,750
  • Buy order sent automatically
Example 2 — Sell GTT
  • You hold RELIANCE at ₹2,800
  • Sell trigger set: ₹2,900
  • RELIANCE rises to ₹2,900
  • Sell order sent automatically

docs.title: GTT Order Status
docs.text: Status Description ActiveStored and waiting for the trigger price to be reached TriggeredTrigger price reached — order has been sent to the exchange FilledOrder completely executed by the exchange Partially FilledOnly part of the order has been executed CancelledGTT order cancelled by the user before being triggered ExpiredGTT order expired before trigger price was reached RejectedExchange rejected the order after it was triggered

docs.title: GTT Order vs Normal Order
docs.text:
NORMAL ORDER
  • Sent to exchange immediately
  • Active only for current trading day
  • Requires manual placement
  • Suitable for immediate trading
→ GTT ORDER
  • Stored until trigger price is reached
  • Stays active till triggered or expired
  • Fires automatically at trigger price
  • Suitable for future price-based trading

docs.title: Advantages & Limitations
docs.text:
Advantages
  • No need to monitor market continuously
  • Automatically places orders at trigger
  • Helps plan trades in advance
  • Reduces emotional trading decisions
  • Suitable for long-term investors
  • Works for both Buy and Sell sides
Limitations
  • Order not sent to exchange until trigger
  • Triggering does not guarantee execution
  • May expire based on broker policy
  • Fast market moves may leave limit unfilled
  • Requires sufficient funds at trigger time

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Buy at Desired Price

Automatically buy a stock when it reaches a specific price.

Sell at Target

Automatically sell holdings when the desired price is reached.

Breakout Trading

Enter a trade when price breaks above or below a level.

Long-Term Investing

Place buy or sell orders in advance without daily monitoring.

!!! tip Always ensure sufficient funds or holdings are available when the trigger fires. Review active GTT orders regularly and cancel unused ones to avoid unintended trades.

docs.title: MTM (Mark-to-Market) Calculation
docs.text:
MTM is the profit or loss on your open position based on the current market price (LTP). It tells you how much you would gain or lose if you closed the position right now.

Real-time P&L Unrealized Profit/Loss F&O Daily Settlement Position Monitoring

docs.title: What is MTM?
docs.text: MTM (Mark-to-Market) is the real-time profit or loss of an open position, calculated using the latest market price (LTP). Since the position has not been closed yet, this is an unrealized profit or loss — it changes continuously as the market price moves.  OPEN POSITION MTM updates live with each LTP change UNREALIZED No actual cash change until position closes CONTINUOUS Recalculated every tick throughout the day

docs.title: MTM Formula
docs.text:
Long (Buy) Position MTM = (LTP − Avg Buy Price) × Quantity

If LTP > Buy Price → ProfitIf LTP < Buy Price → Loss

Short (Sell) Position MTM = (Avg Sell Price − LTP) × Quantity

If LTP < Sell Price → ProfitIf LTP > Sell Price → Loss

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Example 1 — Long Position (Profit) PROFIT StockABC Ltd. Quantity100 shares Avg Buy Price₹500 Current LTP₹530 MTM = (530 − 500) × 100 = ₹30 × 100 MTM = +₹3,000 Profit Example 2 — Long Position (Loss) LOSS StockABC Ltd. Quantity100 shares Avg Buy Price₹500 Current LTP₹480 MTM = (480 − 500) × 100 = −₹20 × 100 MTM = −₹2,000 Loss Example 3 — Short Position (Profit) PROFIT StockABC Ltd. Quantity100 shares Avg Sell Price₹500 Current LTP₹470 MTM = (500 − 470) × 100 = ₹30 × 100 MTM = +₹3,000 Profit Example 4 — Short Position (Loss) LOSS StockABC Ltd. Quantity100 shares Avg Sell Price₹500 Current LTP₹520 MTM = (500 − 520) × 100 = −₹20 × 100 MTM = −₹2,000 Loss

docs.title: How MTM Changes with LTP
docs.text:
You bought 100 shares at ₹500. Watch how MTM moves with price:

Current LTP MTM Status ₹490 −₹1,000 Loss ₹500 ₹0 Break-even ₹510 +₹1,000 Profit ₹520 +₹2,000 Profit ₹540 +₹4,000 Profit

docs.title: MTM vs Realized P&L
docs.text:
📊 MTM (Mark-to-Market)
  • Calculated on open positions
  • Changes with every market price movement
  • Unrealized profit or loss
  • No cash impact until position is closed
✅ Realized P&L
  • Calculated after position is closed
  • Fixed once the trade is completed
  • Actual booked profit or loss
  • Cash is credited/debited to account

Transition Example:

Buy 100 shares @ ₹500 → LTP = ₹520MTM = +₹2,000 → Sell @ ₹520Realized = +₹2,000 | MTM = ₹0

docs.title: Why MTM is Important
docs.text: Shows your real-time profit or loss on every open position Helps you monitor open positions and decide to hold or exit Used in F&O daily settlement by exchanges Assists in managing overall trading risk across positions Helps plan entries and exits based on current P&L Improves discipline — you always know where you stand

docs.title: Real-Life Example — Anita
docs.text:
Anita buys 200 shares of XYZ Ltd. at ₹150 at market open.

LTP rises to ₹160 MTM = (160 − 150) × 200      = ₹10 × 200 +₹2,000 Profit LTP falls to ₹145 MTM = (145 − 150) × 200      = −₹5 × 200 −₹1,000 Loss

Anita has not sold the shares — her MTM keeps updating with every price tick.

In Simple Words: MTM (Mark-to-Market) is the current profit or loss on an open position. It is calculated using the latest market price (LTP) and keeps updating as the market price changes. Once the position is closed, the MTM converts into Realized P&L.

docs.title: MTM Calculation
docs.text:
MTM represents the realized and unrealized profit or loss calculated using the user's current position and the instrument's Last Traded Price (LTP). MTM values are not provided in Interactive API responses; users must compute MTM on their end using current position data that can be fetched by GET Position api or Position data received on Interactive websocket. LastTradedPrice for a particular instrument can be fetched using marketdata apis & websocket. Refer to the sample logic provided below.

openBuyQty = int(position["OpenBuyQuantity"]) openSellQty = int(position["OpenSellQuantity"]) # Realized MTM def safe_div(numerator, denominator): return float(numerator) / float(denominator) if denominator else 0.0 if openBuyQty == 0 or openSellQty == 0: realizedMTM = 0.0 else: totalSquaredOffQuantity = min(openBuyQty, openSellQty) sellWeightedAvgPrice = safe_div(position["SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceSell"], openSellQty) buyWeightedAvgPrice = safe_div(position["SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceBuy"], openBuyQty) realizedMTM = ( totalSquaredOffQuantity * (sellWeightedAvgPrice - buyWeightedAvgPrice) * (float(position["Multiplier"]) * PriceNumerator / PriceDenominator) ) # Unrealized MTM if int(position["Quantity"]) > 0: lastPrice = lastPrice if lastPrice and lastPrice != 0 else closePrice squareOfPrice = lastPrice if squareOfPrice == 0.0: unRealizedMTM = 0.0 else: buyWeightedAvgPrice = float(position["SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceBuy"]) / float(position["OpenBuyQuantity"]) unRealizedMTM = abs(int(position["Quantity"])) * (squareOfPrice - buyWeightedAvgPrice) * (float(position["Multiplier"]) * PriceNumerator / PriceDenominator) else: lastPrice = lastPrice if lastPrice and lastPrice != 0 else closePrice squareOfPrice = lastPrice if squareOfPrice == 0.0: unRealizedMTM = 0.0 else: sellWeightedAvgPrice = float(position["SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceSell"]) / float(position["OpenSellQuantity"]) if not sellWeightedAvgPrice or sellWeightedAvgPrice != sellWeightedAvgPrice: sellWeightedAvgPrice = 0.0 unRealizedMTM = ( abs(int(position["Quantity"])) * (sellWeightedAvgPrice - squareOfPrice) * (float(position["Multiplier"]) * PriceNumerator / PriceDenominator) ) totalMTM = realizedMTM + unRealizedMTM Copy Show Full

docs.title: Margin Calculator
docs.text:
Estimate the margin required before placing a trade — based on exchange, product type, quantity, and price — to ensure you have sufficient funds in your account.

Instant Calculation All Segments Risk Management Pre-trade Margin

docs.title: What is Margin?
docs.text: Margin is the minimum amount of funds required in your account to place or hold a trade. It acts as a security deposit to cover potential losses. The exchange sets margin requirements based on the instrument, product type, and market volatility.

docs.title: Simple Example — RELIANCE MIS Trade
docs.text:
INSTRUMENT RELIANCE EXCHANGE NSECM QUANTITY 100 PRICE ₹2,850 PRODUCT MIS Estimated Required Margin ₹57,000

The calculated amount is an estimate of the funds required to place this trade successfully.

docs.title: Types of Margin
docs.text: S SPAN Margin Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk. The minimum margin required by the exchange for F&O positions, calculated based on the worst possible loss scenario. E Exposure Margin An additional buffer collected by the exchange over SPAN margin to cover mark-to-market losses and other risks not captured by SPAN. V VAR Margin Value at Risk margin applies to equity cash (CNC/MIS) positions. Computed based on the stock's historical price volatility over a defined period. E ELM Margin Extreme Loss Margin is collected to cover losses beyond VAR. It is a fixed percentage set by the exchange for each security.

docs.title: How Margin Calculation Works
docs.text: 👤     Select Instrument    → ⚙️     Enter Trade Details    → 🧮     Margin Calculation    → 💰     Required Margin

docs.title: Why Margin Matters
docs.text:
Avoid insufficient margin errors before placing orders Plan trades by knowing exact fund requirements upfront Supports Equity, F&O, Currency, and Commodity Saves time with instant pre-trade estimates Helps manage risk across multiple positions Improves overall trading discipline and planning

In Simple Words: Margin is the security deposit you must have in your account before placing a trade. The Margin Calculator API lets you check this requirement instantly before submitting any order.
