docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Rate limiting controls the number of requests a client can make to an API within a specific time period — maintaining platform stability, ensuring fair usage, and protecting backend services from excessive traffic.

Per-second limits 429 Too Many Requests Rate-limit headers Unified throttle Exponential backoff Fair resource allocation

docs.title: Why Rate Limiting Is Important
docs.text:
Prevent Overload

Stops servers from being overwhelmed during peak traffic periods.

Fair Usage

Ensures equal resource allocation among all users and clients.

Reliability

Maintains consistent API performance and platform availability.

Abuse Protection

Guards against accidental loops, bots, and excessive automation.

docs.title: How Rate Limits Work
docs.text:
Each endpoint is assigned a maximum number of requests allowed per second (RPS). Requests beyond the limit are rejected until the window resets.

✅ Allowed — 10 req/sec limit Request 1  → ✓ Request 2  → ✓ Request 3  → ✓ ⋮ (up to 10) Request 10 → ✓

10 requests within 1 second — accepted

❌ Rejected — 10 req/sec limit Request 1–10 → ✓ Request 11   → ✗ 429 Request 12   → ✗ 429 Request 13   → ✗ 429 Request 14   → ✗ 429

15 requests within 1 second — 5 rejected

docs.title: Rate Limit Response
docs.text:
When the rate limit is exceeded the API returns HTTP 429:

429 Too Many Requests 
{
  "type": "error",
  "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
  "description": "Request rate exceeded the allowed limit. Please retry after some time."
}

docs.title: Rate Limit Headers
docs.text:
X-RateLimit-Limit Maximum requests allowed per window X-RateLimit-Remaining Remaining requests in the current window X-RateLimit-Reset Unix timestamp when the limit resets EXAMPLE RESPONSE HEADERS 
X-RateLimit-Limit: 10
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 3
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718700000

docs.title: Rate Limits Table
docs.text: API Name Endpoint Method Limit (Req/Sec) Unified Order API Throttle Limit Unified Order API Throttle Limit See Note ↓ 10 Balance /user/balance GET 1 Profile /user/profile GET 1 Brokerage Calculator /user/calculatebrokerage POST 10 Cancel All /orders/cancelall POST 1 Orderbook / Order History /orders GET 1 Tradebook /orders/trades GET 1 Spread Orderbook /orders/spread GET 1 Place GTT Order /orders/gttorder POST 1 Modify GTT Order /orders/gttorder PUT 1 Cancel GTT Order /orders/gttorder DELETE 1 GTT Orderbook /orders/gttorderbook GET 1 Holding /portfolio/holdings GET 1 Position /portfolio/positions GET 1 Position Convert /portfolio/positions/convert PUT 10 Regular Order Margin /orders/margindetails POST 10 Regular Order Modify Margin /orders/modifyordermargindetails POST 10 Cover Order Margin /orders/comargindetails POST 10 Cover Order Modify Margin /orders/comodifymargindetails POST 10 Bracket Order Margin /orders/bomargindetails POST 10 Exchange Status /status/exchange GET 1 Exchange Message /messages/exchange GET 1 Note — Unified Order Throttle Limit:   This is a combined rate limit applied across all order-related APIs listed below.   The standard limit is 10 requests per second, shared cumulatively among these APIs: Place Order, Modify Order, Cancel Order, Place BO (Bracket Order), Modify BO, Cancel BO, Place CO (Cover Order), Exit Cover, Place Spread Order, Modify Spread Order, Cancel Spread Order.

docs.title: Unified Order Throttle Limit
docs.text:
Certain order-management APIs share a combined throttle limit — the total across all three endpoints cannot exceed 10 req/second.

Unified Order APIs POSTPlace Order PUTModify Order DELETECancel Order Shared limit: 10 requests/second Example — Limit Exceeded Place Order  → 5 req Modify Order → 3 req Cancel Order → 4 req Total          = 12 req/sec → Rate limit exceeded (max 10)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Exponential Backoff

On 429, wait 1s → retry. If still failing, wait 2s → 4s → 8s before each retry.

Cache Responses

Cache frequently requested data (e.g., instruments, profile) to avoid redundant API calls.

Monitor Headers

Read X-RateLimit-Remaining before sending batches to stay within limits.

Queue Requests

Queue non-critical requests and spread them over time rather than bursting all at once.

Avoid Polling

Use WebSocket streaming instead of repeatedly polling REST endpoints for updates.

⏱ Respect Retry Intervals

Wait the duration specified by the API in the retry response before re-sending.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Rate limits may vary by endpoint — always check the endpoint-specific table.
  • Limits are subject to change to ensure platform stability.
  • Repeated violations may result in temporary throttling or access restrictions.

docs.title: Socket Streaming
docs.text:
Socket Streaming is a way to receive live, real-time data from the server without sending repeated requests. Once connected, the server automatically pushes new data whenever it becomes available.

Real-time Data Persistent Connection Low Latency Live Trading Ready

docs.title: What is Socket Streaming?
docs.text: Socket Streaming is a real-time communication method where the server continuously pushes live data to the client over a single, always-open connection. You connect once, and the server sends updates automatically — no repeated requests needed.  CONNECT ONCE Open a single persistent connection to the server SERVER PUSHES Server automatically sends updates as they happen INSTANT UPDATES Zero wait — data arrives the moment it changes

docs.title: Why Use Socket Streaming?
docs.text:
Without Socket Streaming (Polling) Client → Request latest price Server → ₹250 Client → Request latest price Server → ₹251 Client → Request latest price Server → ₹249

Many API requests — even when data has not changed.

With Socket Streaming Client ───────────────► Server        Connect Once Server ─► ₹250 Server ─► ₹251 Server ─► ₹249 Server ─► ₹252

Server automatically pushes updates as prices change.

docs.title: How Socket Streaming Works
docs.text: Application Starts ▼ Connect to WebSocket Server ▼ Connection Established ▼ Subscribe to Required Data ▼ Server Sends Live Updates ▼ Application Updates Screen Instantly

docs.title: Example in a Trading Application
docs.text:
Suppose you subscribe to ABC Ltd. The server pushes prices automatically throughout the session:

Time Event Price 9:15:00 AMMarket opens — first tick received₹500 9:15:03 AMPrice update pushed by server₹501 ▲ 9:15:07 AMPrice update pushed by server₹499 ▼ 9:15:12 AMPrice update pushed by server₹503 ▲ No API requests were made after the initial connection — all updates delivered automatically.

docs.title: Data That Can Be Streamed
docs.text: Live stock prices (LTP) Market depth (Bid / Ask)  OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close)  Volume & market statistics Index values (NIFTY, SENSEX) Order status updates  Trade confirmations Position updates Portfolio updates

docs.title: REST API vs Socket Streaming
docs.text: REST API Request → Response Client requests data from server One request returns one response Suitable for static or occasional data Requires repeated API calls for updates Higher latency for live updates Socket Streaming Connect Once → Receive Always Server pushes data automatically One connection delivers continuous updates Designed for live market data No repeated requests after connection Very low latency

docs.title: Advantages of Socket Streaming
docs.text: Real-time updates Faster than polling Lower network overhead Reduced server load Better user experience Ideal for live trading

docs.title: Things to Remember
docs.text: The connection stays open until it is closed or disconnected by either side. If the connection drops, the client should reconnect automatically. You must subscribe to specific symbols or data types after connecting. Multiple symbols can be streamed over the same single connection.

docs.title: Real-Life Analogy — Cricket Match
docs.text: REST API — Refreshing Scorecard        Like refreshing a webpage every 10 seconds to see the latest cricket score. You get the score, but only when you ask — and you may miss updates in between.       Socket Streaming — Live TV        Like watching the match live on TV. The score updates the instant a wicket falls or a run is scored — no refresh needed, no delay.

docs.title: Socket Streaming in RMoney Market Data API
docs.text:
The RMoney Market Data API uses socket streaming to deliver live market data across all subscribed instruments.

LIVE QUOTES Real-time price updates for subscribed instruments MARKET DEPTH Best bid and ask prices with available quantities OHLC UPDATES Open, High, Low, and Close prices streamed live VOLUME Total traded volume and other market statistics INDEX UPDATES Live values of NIFTY, SENSEX, and other indices MULTI-SYMBOL Stream multiple instruments over one connection

docs.title: Typical Flow
docs.text:
Connect to WebSocket ▼ Authenticate (if required) ▼ Subscribe to Instruments ▼ Receive Live Market Data ▼ Unsubscribe or Disconnect

In Simple Words: Socket Streaming lets your application receive live updates over a single, continuous connection. Once connected, the server automatically sends new market data — such as prices, orders, or positions — as soon as it changes, making it ideal for real-time trading applications.

docs.title: Establishment of socket connection
docs.text:
import socketio url = "https://developers.symphonyfintech.in"    # base url userID = "RM"        #userID received from login api token = "xxxxxx"        #Token generated from login api apiType = "INTERACTIVE" socketio_path = "/1interactive/socket.io"        #note:- /1interactive is endpoint you have recieved from hostlookup load balance step logger = False # or "True" sio = socketio.Client() if __name__ == "__main__": try: connectionString = f"{url}?token={token}&userID={userID}&apiType={apiType}" sio.connect(url=connectionString, socketio_path=socketio_path, transports=["websocket"]) sio.wait() except KeyboardInterrupt: print("Stopping client...") sio.disconnect() except Exception as e: print("Connection failed:", e) Copy Show Full Note:
  • XTS uses Socket.io protocol for the Interactive order related data.
  • Users must note that some programming languages does not support socket.io protocol directly, so they need to find compatible websocket libraries.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
This event triggers when socket connection is successfull.

@sio.on("connect") def connect(): print("Connection Established") Copy

docs.title: Joined
docs.text:
If a successful connection is established with the server, this event will be raised to indicate that the user has been connected.

docs.title: Error
docs.text:
In case of any error with the server, this event will be raised along with the cause of the error. For example, if you send an incorrect token while connecting, the server will raise this event and disconnect your socket connection.

@sio.on("error") def on_error(data): print("Error", data) Copy

docs.title: Disconnect
docs.text:
In case a socket disconnection occurs with the server, this event will be raised to indicate the disconnection.

@sio.on("disconnect") def on_disconnect(): print("Disconnected") Copy

docs.title: Spread Orders
docs.text:
A Spread Order places two related positions (legs) simultaneously — one buy and one sell — to profit from the price difference between two instruments rather than the movement of a single one.

Two-leg order Reduced market risk Simultaneous execution Price spread trading F&O strategies Efficient execution

docs.title: Two Legs of a Spread Order
docs.text:
BUY LEG Buy Leg

The instrument you want to buy.

Buy NIFTY July Future ⇄ SELL LEG Sell Leg

The related instrument you want to sell.

Sell NIFTY August Future

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: Create Spread Order → Select Buy Leg → Select Sell Leg → Sent to Exchange → Both Legs Executed

docs.title: Example — NIFTY Calendar Spread
docs.text:
Leg Action Instrument Buy Leg BUY NIFTY July Future Sell Leg SELL NIFTY August Future

If the price difference (spread) between July and August contracts changes in your favor, you make a profit — even if the overall market moves only slightly.

docs.title: Spread Order vs Normal Order
docs.text:
NORMAL ORDER
  • Single buy or sell order
  • Trades one instrument
  • Higher market exposure
  • Regular equity & derivative trading
→ SPREAD ORDER
  • Two linked orders (buy + sell)
  • Trades price difference between two instruments
  • Lower market risk
  • Futures & options strategies

docs.title: Advantages & Limitations
docs.text:
Advantages
  • Reduces overall market risk
  • Both legs executed together
  • Suitable for F&O strategies
  • Profit from price differences
  • No need for multiple separate orders
Limitations
  • Supported on select exchanges only
  • Both instruments must be related
  • More complex than a regular order
  • Requires spread strategy knowledge

docs.title: Common Use Cases!!! tip
docs.text:
📅 Calendar Spread

Buy one month's futures and sell another month's futures contract.

🏭 Commodity Spread

Trade the price difference between two related commodity contracts.

📊 Options Spread

Combine multiple option contracts to manage risk and potential profit.

⚖️ Arbitrage Trading

Take advantage of price differences between related instruments or markets.

Always choose related instruments, ensure sufficient margin for both positions, and verify exchange support before placing a Spread Order.

docs.title: Sample Request and Response
Best Practices
docs.text:
Always Use HTTPS

Never use plain HTTP. HTTPS encrypts all data in transit including your access token.

Include Authorization Header

Every protected endpoint requires your session token in the Authorization header.

Validate Responses

Always check the type field — even a 200 OK can contain a business-logic error.

Handle Rate Limits

Add delays between bulk requests. Avoid hammering endpoints — use WebSocket for live data instead.

Handle Error Codes

Map all HTTP status codes (401, 429, 500, etc.) to appropriate retry or alert logic in your app.

Store Base URL in Config

Never hardcode the base URL. Store it in environment variables so switching environments is instant.

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text:
When an API request fails, RMoney returns an error code with a message so you can identify the problem and fix it fast. Understanding error codes is essential to building reliable trading applications.

Identify problems quickly without guessing Debug API requests with precise context Handle failures gracefully in your application Improve overall application reliability

docs.title: How Errors Work
docs.text: Your Application API Request RMoney API Success Response Data Failure Error Code + Message

docs.title: Error Response Format
docs.text:
Every error response from the RMoney API follows this consistent structure:

{
  "type":        "error",
  "code":        "InvalidInput",
  "description": "Quantity must be greater than zero",
  "result":      {}
}
type Always "error" when the request fails code Short machine-readable error identifier description Human-readable explanation of the error result Empty object on failure

docs.title: 2xx — Success Responses
docs.text:
2xx Request completed successfully These are not errors — they confirm everything went right. 200 OK Request completed. Data is in the response. 
{ "type": "success", "result": { ... } }
201 Created Resource was created (e.g. order placed). 
{ "type": "success", "result": { "AppOrderID": 1234 } }
204 No Content Successful but no response body (e.g. logout). 
HTTP 204 — empty body

docs.title: 4xx — Client Errors
docs.text:
4xx Problem with your request Fix the request before retrying — these errors won't resolve on their own. 400 Bad Request The API cannot understand the request due to invalid or missing data. Missing required fields Invalid parameter format Incorrect data types 
{ "type": "error", "code": "InvalidInput",
  "description": "Invalid Request Parameters" }
401 Unauthorized Authentication failed. The request has no valid access token. Missing Authorization header Invalid token value Token has expired 
{ "type": "error", "code": "Unauthorized",
  "description": "Unauthorized Access" }
403 Forbidden Token is valid but you don't have permission for this resource. Account not enabled for F&O Segment access not granted 
{ "type": "error", "code": "Forbidden",
  "description": "Access Denied" }
404 Not Found The requested endpoint or resource does not exist. Typo in the endpoint path Order ID does not exist 
{ "type": "error", "code": "NotFound",
  "description": "Resource Not Found" }
405 Method Not Allowed The HTTP method used is not supported for this endpoint. Used POST on a GET-only endpoint Wrong HTTP verb in the request 
{ "type": "error", "code": "MethodNotAllowed",
  "description": "Method Not Allowed" }
429 Too Many Requests You have exceeded the allowed number of API calls per second or minute. Sending requests in a tight loop Polling instead of using WebSocket 
{ "type": "error", "code": "RateLimitExceeded",
  "description": "Too Many Requests" }

docs.title: 5xx — Server Errors
docs.text:
5xx Problem on the server side Not caused by your request. Retry with exponential backoff — usually temporary. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected failure inside the API server. 
{ "description": "Internal Server Error" }
502 Bad Gateway Server received an invalid response from an upstream service. 
{ "description": "Bad Gateway" }
503 Service Unavailable API is down for maintenance or overloaded. Retry later. 
{ "description": "Service Temporarily Unavailable" }
504 Gateway Timeout Server took too long to respond. Retry with a smaller request. 
{ "description": "Gateway Timeout" }

docs.title: Common Trading API Errors
docs.text:
Insufficient Funds Not enough balance or margin to place the order. 
{ "description": "Insufficient Funds" }
Invalid Symbol Trading symbol not found in the exchange segment. 
{ "description": "Symbol Not Found" }
Market Closed Request sent outside trading hours. Exchange is closed. 
{ "description": "Market is Closed" }
Invalid Quantity Order quantity is zero, negative, or not a valid lot size. 
{ "description": "Invalid Quantity" }
Order Rejected Exchange or RMS rejected the order after it was sent. 
{ "description": "Order Rejected by Exchange" }
Token Expired Login session expired. Re-authenticate to continue. 
{ "description": "Access Token Expired" }

docs.title: Error Handling Best Practices
docs.text:
Validate Inputs Before Calling

Check all required fields, types, and quantity values before sending the request. A 400 error means the problem is in your request, not the server.

Required fields are present Quantities are positive integers Exchange segment codes are valid Handle 401 Proactively

Don't wait for a 401 response. Track your token's issue time and refresh it before the 24-hour window expires.

Receive 401 Unauthorized Use Refresh Token to re-authenticate Retry original request with new token Retry Temporary Failures with Backoff

Server errors (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) are usually temporary. Use exponential backoff to avoid overwhelming the server.

Retry 1 1 second Retry 2 2 seconds Retry 3 4 seconds Give up Alert user

docs.title: Error Code Summary
docs.text: 2xx Success 200OK — request completed 201Created — resource was made 204No Content — success, no body 4xx Client Errors 400Bad Request — fix your input 401Unauthorized — re-authenticate 403Forbidden — access denied 404Not Found — wrong endpoint or ID 405Method Not Allowed — wrong HTTP verb 429Rate Limited — slow down requests 5xx Server Errors 500Server Error — retry with backoff 502Bad Gateway — retry 503Unavailable — wait and retry 504Timeout — retry smaller request

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Interactive API Overview

The Interactive API allows developers to connect their applications with the RMoney trading platform. Using these APIs, you can authenticate users, retrieve account information, place and manage orders, access portfolio details, and build custom trading applications.

Secure user authentication Place and manage orders Access portfolio information Retrieve account and positions Real-time operations Seamless integration

docs.title: What  is Interactive API?
docs.text: Interactive APIs enable two-way communication between your application and the RMoney trading system. Unlike Market Data APIs that only provide information, Interactive APIs allow you to perform actions such as placing orders, modifying trades, and managing portfolios.

docs.title: Cancel Order API
docs.text: Stop a pending or open order before the exchange executes it. Send the Order ID — the broker cancels it and releases your blocked margin back to your account.

docs.title: Which Orders Can Be Cancelled?
docs.text: Open Order BUY RELIANCE @ ₹2850 — Status: Open Order is live in the exchange order book. Can be cancelled. Pending / New Order SELL TCS @ ₹4200 — Status: New Order just placed, not yet matched. Can be cancelled. Completely Filled Order BUY INFY @ ₹1600 — Status: Filled Trade already executed. Cannot be cancelled. Already Cancelled Order Status: Cancelled Order already cancelled. Duplicate request rejected.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Wrong Order Placement

Accidentally placed 100 shares instead of 10? Cancel the order immediately before it executes.

Market Conditions Changed

Stock price is moving against your expectation. Cancel the pending order and avoid unwanted trades.

Better Price Available

Cancel the existing limit order and place a new one at a better price to improve your entry.

Risk Management

Remove unwanted pending orders during highly volatile sessions to control exposure.

docs.title: Partial Fill Scenario
docs.text:
Original Order 
BUY 100 Shares of RELIANCE
Status = Partially Filled
Executed = 60 Shares
Remaining = 40 Shares
After Cancel Request 
Executed 60 shares → Remain valid
Remaining 40 shares → Cancelled

Final Status: Partially Filled → Cancelled
Margin for 40 shares released back

When you cancel a partially filled order, only the remaining unfilled quantity is cancelled. The already-executed shares are locked and cannot be undone.

docs.title: Order Life Cycle
docs.text: Successful Cancellation New ↓ Open ↓ Cancel Request ↓ Cancelled Already Executed New ↓ Open ↓ Filled ↓ Cancel Rejected Partial Fill Cancel New ↓ Open ↓ Partially Filled ↓ Partial → Cancelled

docs.title: Advanced Concepts
docs.text:
Exchange Validation

Before cancelling, the exchange checks the current order status, whether it has already been matched, and whether cancellation is allowed for that order type.

Risk Management System

Broker systems verify user permissions, order ownership, and any exchange-level restrictions before forwarding the cancel request.

Margin Release

After successful cancellation, the funds or margins that were blocked for the order are released back to the user's available balance.

Race Condition

If the order executes at the exact same moment as your cancel request, the cancel may be rejected and the trade will have gone through. Always check the final status.

docs.title: Cancel All Orders
docs.text:
Cancel All Orders

Cancel All Orders cancels all your active (open or pending) orders at once with a single request — no need to cancel each order individually. Especially useful during volatile markets or when exiting all positions quickly.

Single request Risk reduction Saves time Volatile markets Multi-order mgmt End of session

docs.title: Which Orders Are Affected?
docs.text:
Can Be Cancelled
  • Open Orders
  • Pending / New Orders
  • Pending Trigger Orders
  • Partially Filled (remaining qty)
Cannot Be Cancelled

docs.title: Cancel All Orders vs Cancel Order
docs.text:
CANCEL ORDER
  • Cancels one specific order
  • Requires individual Order ID
  • Best for single order removal
→ CANCEL ALL ORDERS
  • Cancels all active orders at once
  • No need to specify Order IDs
  • Best for fast exits & risk control

docs.title: Advantages & Limitations
docs.text:
Advantages
  • Cancel multiple orders instantly
  • Saves time in busy sessions
  • Reduces market exposure quickly
  • Prevents accidental executions
  • Easier order management
Limitations
  • Filled orders cannot be cancelled
  • Orders mid-execution may still fill
  • Depends on exchange acceptance
  • Cannot undo after execution

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Market Volatility

Cancel all pending orders during sudden market movements to avoid unwanted fills.

End of Session

Remove all unexecuted orders before the market closes.

Strategy Change

Cancel all existing orders before placing new ones with updated strategy.

Risk Management

Quickly reduce exposure by cancelling all pending orders at once.

!!! warning Review your active orders before using Cancel All Orders. Orders already being executed may still get filled before the cancellation is processed. Use carefully during live trading.

docs.title: Order Sides
docs.text:
BUY

Purchase shares from the market.

BUY 10 shares of RELIANCE

Money decreases → Shares added to holdings

SELL

Sell shares back to the market.

SELL 5 shares of RELIANCE

Shares decrease → Money credited to account

docs.title: Order Types
docs.text:
MARKET

Executes immediately at current market price. Price may vary slightly due to market fluctuation.

Use when: Speed matters more than exact price BUY 10 RELIANCE (Market) → executed at ₹2849.80 or ₹2850.10 LIMIT

Executes only at your specified price. Order waits until price is reached.

Use when: Price matters more than speed BUY RELIANCE @ ₹2840 → waits until price drops to ₹2840 STOP LOSS

Activates a sell order automatically when price drops to your trigger price. Limits your loss.

Use when: Protecting against sudden price drops Bought at ₹2850 → Trigger ₹2800 → auto-sells if price falls

docs.title: Product Types
docs.text:
MIS Margin Intraday Square-off

Position must be closed on the same day.

Buy at 10 AM → Sell before market closes CNC Cash and Carry

Delivery trading. Shares stay in your Demat account.

Buy today → Hold for months or years NRML Normal

Carry forward position. Used mostly in Futures & Options.

F&O positions carried overnight

docs.title: Time In Force
docs.text:
DAY

Order remains valid for the current trading day. Cancelled at end of session if unfilled.

IOC

Immediate Or Cancel. Execute instantly. Any unexecuted portion is cancelled immediately.

Status: Partially Filled Slippage

Expected ₹2850 but executed at ₹2850.30. The ₹0.30 difference is slippage — common with Market orders.

Margin Check

docs.title: Funds Overview
docs.text:
Funds represent the money available in your trading account. They determine buying power, margin utilisation, and whether you can place new orders.

Trading Wallet= Funds Credit Limit= Margin Available Blocked Amount= Pending Orders

docs.title: What are Funds?
docs.text:
Funds are like the wallet of your trading account. They show how much money you have, how much is being used, and how much is still free for trading. Without sufficient funds, orders cannot be placed.

Real-Life Example Total₹1,00,000 In Stocks₹20,000 Blocked₹10,000 Free₹70,000 ↔ Funds API Returns Cash BalanceTotal deposited Used MarginBlocked for trades AvailableReady to trade Buying PowerWith leverage

docs.title: Why are Funds Important?
docs.text: Know how much money is available for trading Manage risk and prevent overtrading Understand margin utilisation at a glance Monitor deposits and withdrawals Check buying power before placing orders Track blocked and available amounts in real time

docs.title: How Funds Flow
docs.text: User Deposits Money ↓ Funds Become Available ↓ User Places Orders ↓ Margin Gets Blocked ↓ Trades Execute ↓ ✅Funds Updated with P&L

docs.title: Fund Components
docs.text:
AVAILABLE BALANCE

Amount currently free for placing new orders.

₹1,00,000 − ₹20,000 used = ₹80,000 available UTILISED MARGIN

Amount blocked by open positions and pending orders.

Order requires ₹15,000 → ₹15,000 gets blocked CASH BALANCE

Actual money deposited via bank transfers, profits, or withdrawals.

Bank transfer → Trading account → Cash balance BUYING POWER

Total trading capacity including broker-provided leverage.

₹50,000 × 5× margin = ₹2,50,000 buying power BLOCKED FUNDS

Amounts reserved for pending orders, margin, and fees — released when order executes or cancels.

Buy 100 @ ₹100 → ₹10,000 blocked until fill/cancel PAY-IN / PAY-OUT

Pay-In is money added today. Pay-Out is money withdrawn today.

Deposit ₹25,000 ↑  |  Withdraw ₹10,000 ↓

docs.title: How P&L Affects Funds
docs.text:
Profit Adds to Funds 
Bought  @ ₹100
Sold    @ ₹120
Profit  = ₹20 per share

→ ₹20 gets ADDED to available balance
Loss Reduces Funds 
Bought  @ ₹100
Sold    @ ₹85
Loss    = ₹15 per share

→ ₹15 gets DEDUCTED from available balance

docs.text: ENDPOINT GET https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/user/balance Requires: valid Authorization token Copy URL

docs.text: FieldDescriptionExample cashAvailableFree cash in the trading account₹50,000 utilisedAmountMargin blocked by open orders/positions₹12,500 netAvailableMarginCash + collateral − used margin₹52,500 collateralValueValue of pledged securities as margin₹15,000 payinMoney added to account today₹0 payoutMoney withdrawn today₹0

docs.title: What Happens Internally?
docs.text: 1User requests fund details — API call with valid session token 2Session validation — broker server verifies auth token 3Ledger data retrieved — cash balance, deposits, withdrawals fetched 4Margin engine calculates usage — sums all blocked amounts from open orders and positions 5Account balances updated — net available margin computed 6Response returned — full structured JSON with all fund fields

docs.title: Advanced Concepts
docs.text:
Margin Leverage

Broker provides extra trading capacity. With 5× leverage, ₹20,000 capital can trade ₹1,00,000 worth of positions.

Realized P&L

Profit from closed trades is added to available funds immediately after the trade settles.

Unrealized P&L

Floating profit/loss on open positions. Not yet in funds — becomes real only when position is closed.

Risk Monitoring

Broker systems continuously check margin, exposure, and losses. Orders are rejected if funds fall below required margin.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Before Placing Orders

Always check available balance before placing large orders to avoid rejection due to insufficient margin.

Risk Management

Monitor margin utilisation and set alerts when available balance falls below a safe threshold.

Withdrawals

Use Pay-Out field to know the withdrawable balance without disturbing active positions.

Margin Trading

Track leveraged positions — ensure enough buffer so broker does not square off positions automatically.

In Simple Words: Funds represent the money available in a trading account. They determine how much a user can trade, how much margin is used, and how much remains available. The Funds API provides a complete view of cash balance, margin, blocked amounts, and buying power — helping users manage their trading efficiently. Think of Funds as the wallet of your trading account, where money flows in and out as trades execute.

docs.title: Holdings
docs.text:
Holdings are the stocks or securities that belong to you and are stored in your demat/investment account. These are your long-term investments and remain until you sell them.

Demat Account Stocks Live P&L Tracking Delivery Only Long-term Investment

docs.title: What are Holdings?
docs.text: Holdings represent the shares that you own in your Demat account after successful delivery. Unlike positions, holdings do not include intraday trades — they only show shares that have been settled and delivered to your Demat account.

docs.title: How Holdings Work
docs.text:
When you buy shares for delivery (CNC), the shares are credited to your Demat account on the settlement day. Once credited, they appear in your Holdings and you can:

Days Hold for a few days Months Hold for several months Years Hold for many years

There is no requirement to sell them on the same day — unlike intraday positions.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
EXAMPLE 1 Buying Delivery Shares

Buy 100 shares of ABC Ltd. at ₹500 (CNC/Delivery)

100 × ₹500 = ₹50,000 StockQtyAvg Price ABC Ltd.100₹500 EXAMPLE 2 Selling Some Shares

You own 100 shares. You sell 30 shares.

−30Sold 70Remain StockQty ABC Ltd.70 EXAMPLE 3 Multiple Purchases

Buy 50 @ ₹500 + Buy 50 @ ₹520

(50×500 + 50×520) ÷ 100 = ₹510 StockQtyAvg Price ABC Ltd.100₹510

docs.title: Information Available in Holdings
docs.text: FieldDescription SymbolStock name or trading symbol ISINUnique identification number assigned to the security ExchangeExchange where the stock is traded (NSE / BSE) QuantityTotal shares currently owned AvailableQuantityShares that can be sold immediately AveragePriceAverage purchase price per share LTPLast Traded Price — current market price of the stock MarketValueCurrent value of your holdings (Quantity × LTP) InvestedValueTotal amount invested (Quantity × Average Price) UnrealizedPnLProfit or loss if you sold the shares at the current market price DayChangeToday's gain or loss based on today's market movement

docs.title: Understanding Key Fields
docs.text:
Quantity

Number of shares you own.

Reliance IndustriesQuantity = 50 shares owned Average Price

Average price at which you bought the shares.

Buy 20 @ ₹100 + Buy 30 @ ₹120 (20×100 + 30×120) ÷ 50 = ₹112 Market Value

Current worth of your holdings.

Market Value = Qty × LTP 100 × ₹550 = ₹55,000 Invested Value

Total money spent to purchase the shares.

Invested Value = Qty × Avg Price 100 × ₹500 = ₹50,000 Unrealized P&L

Profit or loss if you sold now. Called unrealized because you haven't sold yet.

P&L = Market Value − Invested Value ₹55,000 − ₹50,000 = +₹5,000 profit ₹48,000 − ₹50,000 = −₹2,000 loss Day Change

Gain or loss during the current trading day.

Yesterday close: ₹540 → Today LTP: ₹550 Day Change = +₹10 × 100 shares = +₹1,000

docs.title: Lifecycle of Holdings
docs.text: Buy Delivery Shares ↓ Order Executed ↓ Settlement Completed ↓ Shares Credited to Demat ↓ Appear in Holdings ↓ Keep or Sell Anytime

docs.title: Holdings vs Positions
docs.text:
HOLDINGS
  • ▸ Shows stocks owned in the Demat account
  • ▸ Only delivery shares are displayed
  • ▸ Shares remain until sold
  • ▸ Used mainly for investing
  • ▸ Cannot have a negative quantity
POSITIONS
  • ▸ Shows active trading positions
  • ▸ Includes intraday, delivery, futures, options
  • ▸ May close on the same day or remain open
  • ▸ Used for tracking trading activity

docs.title: What is a Portfolio?
docs.text:
A portfolio is a digital folder that holds all the stocks, mutual funds, bonds, and other securities owned by an investor. Just like a bank statement shows your money, the portfolio shows all your investments in one place.

Real-Life Example 20 sharesReliance Industries 10 sharesTCS 50 sharesHDFC Bank Together= Your Portfolio ↔ What Portfolio API Gives HoldingsStocks you own PositionsActive open trades Market ValueCurrent worth P&LProfit or Loss

docs.title: Why is Portfolio Important?
docs.text: Track all investments in one place Monitor profit and loss in real time Understand current holdings and their value Measure overall investment performance Make better, data-driven decisions Diversify risk across different assets

docs.title: Portfolio Workflow
docs.text: User Makes API Request ↓ Broker Server ↓ Account Database ↓ Holdings & Positions Retrieved ↓ P&L Calculated ↓ ✅Portfolio Data Returned

docs.title: Portfolio Components
docs.text:
HOLDINGS

Stocks and securities you currently own in your Demat account. Remain until you sell them.

Reliance × 20 | TCS × 10 | Infosys × 15 POSITIONS

Currently active trades — intraday (Day) and carry-forward (Net) positions.

Buy Reliance @ ₹2800 → hold / sell same day AVERAGE PRICE

Average cost per share across multiple buy transactions.

(10×₹100 + 10×₹120) ÷ 20 = ₹110 MARKET VALUE

Current worth of your holdings at live market price.

20 shares × ₹2900 = ₹58,000 INVESTED VALUE

Total amount you originally paid to buy the shares.

20 shares × ₹2800 = ₹56,000 P&L

Profit or loss — difference between Market Value and Invested Value.

₹58,000 − ₹56,000 = ₹2,000 Profit

docs.title: Position Types
docs.text:
Day Position

Intraday trades opened and closed on the same trading day.

Buy Reliance @ ₹2800 → Sell @ ₹2820 same day

Profit = ₹20 per share (Realized)

Net Position

Positions carried forward beyond the current trading session.

Buy TCS today → Hold for several days

Profit is Unrealized until you sell

docs.title: What Happens Internally?
docs.text: 1User requests portfolio — API call with valid session token 2Portfolio API validates session — checks auth token 3Broker server fetches data — holdings and positions from database 4Market prices retrieved — live LTP fetched for each instrument 5P&L calculated — realized and unrealized computed per position 6Portfolio data returned — full structured JSON response

docs.title: P&L Formulas
docs.text:
Realized P&L Profit / loss from closed trades

Locked in when you complete a trade — Buy + Sell same stock.

FORMULA Realized P&L = (Sell Price − Buy Price) × Qty EXAMPLE Bought @₹100 Sold @₹120 Profit+₹20 per share Unrealized P&L Floating profit / loss on open positions

Fluctuates with market price. Not in funds until position is closed.

FORMULA Long  : P&L = (LTP − Avg Buy Price) × Open Qty Short : P&L = (Avg Sell Price − LTP) × Open Qty EXAMPLE (LONG) Bought Reliance @₹2,800 Current LTP₹2,900 Unrealized+₹100 per share

Investment Tracking

docs.text:
Concentrated Risk

100% in one sector — if that sector crashes, your entire portfolio suffers.

₹1,00,000 → All in IT stocks Diversified

Spread across sectors — one sector falls but others can offset the loss.

Banking 25% | IT 25% | Pharma 25% | FMCG 25% In Simple Words: A Portfolio is a complete collection of all investments owned by a user. Portfolio APIs return holdings, positions, investment value, market value, and profit or loss — allowing traders and apps to track and manage investments efficiently. Think of it as a report card for your investments, showing where your money is and how it is performing.

docs.title: Position Convert
docs.text:
Change the product type of an open position without closing the trade — for example, convert Intraday (MIS) to Delivery (CNC) to hold overnight.

No Re-entry Needed MIS → CNC / NRML Avoid Auto Square-off Qty & P&L Preserved

docs.title: What is Position Convert?
docs.text: Position Convert is the process of changing the product type of an existing open position without closing the trade. Only the product category changes — the stock, quantity, buy/sell price, and P&L all remain the same.

docs.title: Why is Position Conversion Needed?
docs.text: Bought intraday but want to hold it for several days Accidentally selected the wrong product type on order placement Want to avoid automatic intraday square-off

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
EXAMPLE 1 Intraday → Delivery

You buy 100 shares of ABC Ltd. at ₹500 as Intraday (MIS). Later you decide to keep them as an investment.

IntradayMIS → DeliveryCNC

Shares will be credited to your Demat after settlement (subject to sufficient funds).

EXAMPLE 2 Delivery → Intraday

You accidentally placed a Delivery (CNC) order but only wanted to trade for the day.

DeliveryCNC → IntradayMIS

Now the trade is treated as an intraday position (if broker allows it).

docs.title: Common Position Conversions
docs.text: FromToNote Intraday (MIS)Delivery (CNC)Most common — hold overnight Delivery (CNC)Intraday (MIS)If allowed by broker MarginDeliveryConvert margin position to delivery DeliveryMarginSubject to broker rules NRMLMISFor derivatives, if supported MISNRMLFor derivatives, if supported

docs.title: What Changes During Conversion?
docs.text:
✔ STAYS THE SAME
  • ● Stock or contract
  • ● Quantity
  • ● Buy / Sell price
  • ● Average price
  • ● P&L (based on market)
✦ WHAT CHANGES
  • ● Product type (MIS / CNC / NRML)
  • ● Margin requirement
  • ● Square-off behavior
  • ● Settlement treatment

docs.title: When Can You Convert?
docs.text: ✔ Position is still open ✔ Market is open (within conversion window) ✔ Sufficient funds or margin available ✔ Exchange and broker support the conversion

docs.title: Position Conversion Workflow
docs.text: Place an Order ↓ Position is Created ↓ Need to Change Product Type? ↓ Submit Position Conversion Request via API ↓ Broker Validates Funds, Margin & Rules ↓ Position Continues with New Product Type ✔

docs.title: Real-Life Example
docs.text:
Rahul buys 100 shares of XYZ Ltd. at ₹300 as Intraday (MIS). By afternoon, the stock is rising and he believes it will continue for a few days. He converts the position.

BEFORE MIS Intraday → AFTER CNC Delivery

Shares are credited to Rahul's Demat after settlement. He can now hold them for as long as he wants.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Avoid automatic intraday square-off Correct an incorrect product selection Hold shares for the long term Adjust strategy without a new order Save time & brokerage on re-entry ⚠️ Things to Remember: Not every position can be converted. Some brokers charge additional fees or require extra margin. Derivative positions (Futures & Options) may have different conversion rules. Once a position is fully closed, it cannot be converted.

In Simple Words: Position Convert means changing the product type of an open position (such as Intraday to Delivery) without closing the trade. This lets you continue holding the same position under a different trading category, subject to your broker's rules.

docs.title: Positions
docs.text:
View and manage your currently active open trades — both intraday (MIS) and overnight (NRML/CNC) positions across all exchange segments.

Day-wise & Net-wise Real-time MTM PnL Product Conversion All Segments

docs.title: What is a Position?
docs.text: A Position shows how many shares or contracts you currently hold in a particular security after all your buy and sell trades. Think of it as a real-time summary of your activity for each stock or instrument.

docs.title: Simple Example — ACC Ltd.
docs.text:
ActionQuantityRunning Position ▲ Buy 100 +100 ▲ Buy 50 +150 ▼ Sell 30 +120

Your current position is 120 shares of ACC Ltd.

docs.title: Types of Positions
docs.text:
▲ Long Position

You have bought more than you sold. You own shares.

Buy 100 sharesSell 20 shares Position: +80 (Long) ▼ Short Position

You have sold more than you bought. Allowed in intraday & derivatives.

Sell 100 sharesBuy 40 shares Position: −60 (Short) ● Closed Position

All bought quantity is sold (or vice versa). No open holding remains.

Buy 100 sharesSell 100 shares Position: 0 (Closed)

docs.title: Position Information
docs.text:
A position entry includes the following key fields:

FieldDescription SymbolName of the stock or contract ExchangeExchange where it is traded — NSE, BSE, MCX, etc. ProductTypeDelivery, Intraday, Margin, Futures, Options, etc. BuyQuantityTotal quantity purchased SellQuantityTotal quantity sold NetQuantityBuy Quantity − Sell Quantity BuyAveragePriceAverage price of all buy trades SellAveragePriceAverage price of all sell trades LTPLast Traded Price — latest market price of the security MTM / P&LCurrent profit or loss based on market price

docs.title: Position vs Holdings
docs.text:
POSITION
  • ▸ Shows your active trading position
  • ▸ Includes intraday and derivative trades
  • ▸ Changes throughout the trading day
  • ▸ Can be Long or Short
HOLDINGS
  • ▸ Shows stocks owned in your Demat account
  • ▸ Only delivery shares are shown
  • ▸ Changes only when delivery is credited/debited
  • ▸ Always represents owned shares

docs.title: Real-Life Example
docs.text:
Imagine you buy 100 shares of XYZ Ltd. at ₹500, then sell 40 shares at ₹520.

BUY QTY 100 SELL QTY 40 NET POSITION 60 MARKET PRICE ₹530

Your remaining 60 shares are valued at the latest price of ₹530. Unrealized P&L = (530 − 500) × 60 = ₹1,800 profit.

docs.title: Why Positions Are Important
docs.text:
Track your current open trades Monitor real-time P&L See quantity you own or need to close Make informed buy/sell decisions Manage risk by monitoring exposure Avoid auto square-off penalties

In Simple Words: A Position is a real-time summary of your trading activity for a particular stock or contract. It shows how many units you currently hold (or owe), along with their current profit or loss.

docs.title: Order Book
docs.text:
A complete record of all buy and sell orders placed in your trading account — including their current status, execution details, and full order lifecycle.

All Order Statuses Real-time Updates Modify & Cancel All Segments

docs.title: What is an Order Book?
docs.text: The Order Book is a record of all the orders you have placed with your trading account. It shows the current status of each order — whether it is pending, executed, cancelled, rejected, or partially filled. An Order Book helps you track every order from the moment it is placed until it is completed or cancelled.  Simple Definition: An Order Book is a list of all your buy and sell orders, along with their current status and details.

docs.title: Why is the Order Book Important?
docs.text: Track all placed orders Check if order is executed or pending View order price & quantity details Modify or cancel eligible orders Monitor partially executed orders Avoid missed or duplicate orders

docs.title: How an Order Moves Through the Order Book
docs.text:
1 Place Order 2 Order Received by Exchange 3 Order Pending — waiting to match 4 Matched with Another Order ✓ Order Executed → Appears in Trade Book & Position

If the order cannot be executed, it may instead become:

Cancelled — user or broker cancelled before execution Rejected — exchange or broker rejected the order

docs.text: Order ID Symbol Side Qty Price Status 10001 ABC Ltd. BUY 100 ₹500 Filled 10002 XYZ Ltd. SELL 50 ₹700 Pending 10003 PQR Ltd. BUY 200 ₹150 Partially Filled 10004 LMN Ltd. SELL 100 ₹400 Cancelled

docs.title: Common Order Statuses
docs.text:
PENDING

The order has been accepted but not yet executed.

Buy 100 shares @ ₹500Current Market Price = ₹505 Status: Pending FILLED

The entire order has been successfully executed.

Buy 100 shares @ ₹500Filled Quantity = 100 Status: Filled PARTIALLY FILLED

Only part of the requested quantity has been executed.

Buy Quantity = 100  |  Executed = 60Remaining = 40 Status: Partially Filled CANCELLED / REJECTED

Cancelled by user/broker, or rejected by exchange due to invalid price, quantity, or insufficient funds.

Buy 100 shares — cancelled before execution Reasons: Insufficient funds · Invalid price · Market closed Status: Cancelled / Rejected

docs.title: Order Book vs Trade Book vs Position
docs.text:
ORDER BOOK
  • ▸Shows all placed orders
  • ▸Includes pending, cancelled & filled
  • ▸Tracks order lifecycle
TRADE BOOK
  • ▸Shows only executed trades
  • ▸Only completed executions
  • ▸Confirms completed trades
POSITION
  • ▸Current open quantity
  • ▸Only executed quantities
  • ▸Tracks current holdings

docs.title: Real-Life Example
docs.text:
Rahul places an order to buy 100 shares of ABC Ltd. at ₹500.

1 Order appears in Order Book — Status: Pending 2 Exchange executes 60 shares — Status: Partially Filled 3 Remaining 40 shares are executed — Status: Filled ✓ Trade appears in Trade Book and Rahul's Position shows 100 shares

In Simple Words: The Order Book is a complete record of all your buy and sell orders. It shows each order's details and current status — Pending, Filled, Partially Filled, Cancelled, or Rejected — so you can monitor every order from placement to completion.

docs.title: Trade Book vs Order Book
docs.text:
ORDER BOOK
  • Shows all orders placed
  • Pending, executed, cancelled & rejected
  • Active orders can be modified or cancelled
  • Used to monitor status of all orders
  • One entry per order
→ TRADE BOOK
  • Shows only executed trades
  • Completed transactions only
  • Cannot modify or cancel trades
  • Used to verify completed trades
  • One row per execution (partial fills = multiple rows)

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Verify Trades

Confirm that a trade has been successfully executed.

Calculate P&L

Use executed prices to calculate trading profit or loss.

Trading History

Keep a record of all completed buy and sell transactions.

Reconcile Orders

Match executed trades with the corresponding orders.

Performance Analysis

Review past trades to evaluate trading performance.

!!! tip If an order was partially filled in multiple executions, you will see multiple rows in the Trade Book for the same AppOrderID — one row per execution.

docs.title: User
docs.text: The User APIs are used for authentication, account management, and retrieving user-specific information. These APIs provide secure access to the RMoney Interactive API and allow applications to manage user sessions and account details.

docs.title: POST Login API
docs.text:
The Login API is used to log in to the trading account. After successful login, it creates a session and allows the user to access Interactive API services.

Example: User logs in before placing orders or checking portfolio details.

It helps the XTS server recognize the origin of the request and apply the appropriate permissions and validations.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Authentication

Authentication (Auth) is the process of verifying a user's identity before allowing access to Market Data APIs — the security check that confirms you are an authorized user.

Secure access Prevents unauthorized use Account protection API usage control Request tracking Valid users only

docs.title: How Authentication Works
docs.text: Send Login Request → Server Validates → Token Generated → Token Returned → API Access Granted

docs.title: Login & Logout APIs
docs.text:
Login (POST)

You are logging in to the authentication using the POST method request. You will receive a token parameter in the response which is used to authenticate subsequent requests. All request headers should have the content type set to application/json.

URL https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/auth/login Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description secretKey RawString Y The predefined secret key assigned to the client appKey RawString Y The App Key issued for the client Request Body JSON { "secretKey": "xxxxxxxxxxxx", "appKey": "xxxxxxxxxxxx" } Response Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Description token Token The authentication token used to authorize every subsequent request userID UserID UserID of the logged-in client appVersion AppVersion Market Data App version application_expiry_date ApplicationExpiryDate Application key expiry date Response Body JSON { "type": "success", "code": "s-response-0010", "description": "Provided Valid Credentials", "result": { "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...", "userID": "DVJ8588", "appVersion": "5.0.15", "application_expiry_date": "30-12-2028" } } Logout (DELETE)

You are logging out of the application using the DELETE method request. You will need to pass the Token/Authorization value in the request header. You will receive a success/failure message in the response.

URL https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/auth/logout Response Body JSON { "type": "success", "code": "s-login-0005", "description": "successfully logged out", "result": {} }

docs.title: Step 1 — Send Login Request
docs.text:
The user provides credentials:

{ "secretKey": "xxxxx", "appKey": "xxxxx", "source": "WebAPI" }

docs.title: Step 2 — Server Validates Credentials
docs.text:
✔ App Key valid?

Checks if the App Key exists and is active.

✔ Secret Key valid?

Matches the Secret Key against stored records.

✔ Access rights?

Confirms the user has permission to access data.

docs.title: Step 3 — Token Generated & Returned
docs.text:
If validation succeeds, the server returns an access token:

{ "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1Ni..." }

docs.title: Step 4 — Use Token in Future Requests
docs.text:
Include the token in every API request header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: What is an Access Token?
docs.text: WITHOUT TOKEN Login every single API call → WITH TOKEN Login once → use token for all calls

docs.title: Authentication Failure Errors
docs.text: Invalid Credentials "type": "error", "description": "Invalid App Key" Expired Token "type": "error", "description": "Session Expired" Unauthorized Access "type": "error", "description": "Authentication Failed"

docs.title: APIs That Require Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is the first API call before accessing any of these:

Real-time Quotes OHLC Data Market Depth Instruments WebSocket Historical Data

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
Keep Keys Private

Never expose App Key, Secret Key, or Access Token in public code or repositories.

Use HTTPS

Always communicate through secure encrypted connections.

Store Tokens Securely

Avoid storing tokens in client-side code or public repositories.

Refresh Expired Sessions

Generate a new token when the current session expires.

docs.title: Real-Life Analogy
docs.text:
Office Building
  • Building = Market Data API
  • ID Card Check = Authentication
  • Access Card = Token
  • Office Entry = API Access
✔ Key Takeaway Without the ID card, you cannot enter the building. Similarly, without authentication, you cannot access market data.

docs.title: Enums With Numeric Constants
docs.text:
Enums with Numeric Constants

Enums are predefined sets of values used by the Market Data API to represent options, states, or configurations — using compact numeric codes for speed and consistency.

docs.title: 1. ExchangeSegments
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description NSECM 1 - NSE Cash Market segment for trading equity shares.- Used to buy and sell stocks listed on NSE.- Example: Reliance, TCS, Infosys shares. NSEFO 2 - NSE Futures & Options segment.- Used for trading futures and options contracts.- Example: NIFTY Futures, BANKNIFTY Options. NSECD 3  - NSE Currency Derivatives segment.- Used for trading currency futures and options.- Example: USD/INR, EUR/INR contracts. NSECO 4 - NSE Commodity segment.- Used for commodity derivative trading on NSE.- Example: Gold, Silver, Crude Oil contracts. BSECM 11  - BSE Cash Market segment for equity trading.- Used to buy and sell stocks listed on BSE.- Example: Stocks traded on the Bombay Stock Exchange. BSEFO 12 - BSE Futures & Options segment.- Used for trading derivative contracts on BSE.- Example: SENSEX Futures and Options. BSECD 13  - BSE Currency Derivatives segment.- Used for trading currency-based derivative contracts.- Example: USD/INR currency futures. MCXFO 51  - MCX Futures & Options segment.- Used for commodity derivatives trading.- Example: Gold, Silver, Crude Oil Futures. NCDEX 21  - National Commodity & Derivatives Exchange segment.- Used mainly for agricultural commodity trading.- Example: Cotton, Soybean, Chana Futures.

docs.title: 2. MarketType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Normal 1 - Represents the regular trading session of the exchange.- Market data is received for normal buy and sell activities.- Most stock and derivative trading happens in this market type. Oddlot 2 - Used for trades involving quantities smaller than the standard market lot.- Commonly used when the quantity does not meet the regular lot size.- Market data is published separately from normal trades. Retaildebt 3 - Represents the retail debt market segment.- Used for trading bonds and other debt securities by retail investors.- Market data includes prices and trades of debt instruments. Auction 4 - Represents the auction market session.- Used for special auction-based trading conducted by the exchange.- Orders are matched through an auction process instead of continuous trading. CallAuction1 5 - Represents the first type of call auction market session.- Orders are collected first and then executed together at a single price.- Commonly used during special auction periods. CallAuction2 6 - Represents the second type of call auction market session.- Similar to CallAuction1, orders are matched in a batch at one price.- Used for specific exchange-defined auction sessions.

docs.title: 3. InstrumentType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Futures 1 - A Futures contract is an agreement to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date.- Traders use it to earn profit from price movements without owning the asset immediately.- It is commonly used for stocks, commodities, currencies, and market indices. Options 2 - An Option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price.- It helps traders manage risk or profit from expected price changes.- The buyer pays a small fee called a premium to get this right. Spread 4 - A Spread means taking two related trading positions at the same time.- One position is bought and the other is sold to reduce risk.- Profit comes from the difference in price movement between the two positions. Equity 8 - Equity represents ownership in a company through shares or stocks.- When you buy equity shares, you become a part-owner of that company.- Your profit can come from share price growth and dividends. Spot 16 - Spot trading means buying or selling an asset immediately at the current market price.- The ownership and payment are usually settled right away.- It is the simplest form of trading used in stocks, currencies, and commodities. PreferenceShares 32 - Preference Shares are special shares that give fixed dividends before equity shareholders are paid.- They usually have lower risk compared to ordinary shares.- However, preference shareholders often have limited or no voting rights. Debentures 64 - Debentures are a type of loan given by investors to a company.- The company promises to pay regular interest and return the money after a fixed period.- Debenture holders are creditors, not owners of the company. Warrants 128 - A Warrant gives the holder the right to buy company shares at a fixed price in the future.- It is usually valid for a longer period than options.- Investors use warrants when they expect the company's share price to rise. Miscellaneous 256 - Miscellaneous includes financial instruments that do not fit into common categories.- These may have unique features, purposes, or trading rules.- Examples can vary depending on the market or financial institution. MutualFund 512 - A Mutual Fund collects money from many investors and invests it in different assets.- Professional fund managers make investment decisions on behalf of investors.- It helps people diversify investments and reduce individual investment risk.

docs.title: 4. XTS Message Code
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description TouchLineEvent 1501 - A TouchLineEvent occurs whenever the latest market price (Last Traded Price) changes.- It provides quick updates about the current trading activity of a stock or instrument.- Traders use it to monitor real-time price movements and market direction. MarketDepthEvent 1502 - A MarketDepthEvent shows the list of buy and sell orders currently available in the market.- It helps traders see demand, supply, and liquidity at different price levels.- This information is useful for understanding market strength and planning trades. CandleDataEvent 1505 - A CandleDataEvent provides price data in candlestick format for a specific time period.- Each candle contains Open, High, Low, and Close (OHLC) prices.- Traders use candlestick data to analyze trends, patterns, and market behavior. OpenInterestEvent 1510 - An OpenInterestEvent shows the total number of active futures or options contracts in the market.- It indicates how much money and participation are present in a particular contract.- Rising open interest often suggests stronger market activity and trader interest.

docs.title: 5. Exchange Trading Session
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description PreOpenStart 0 - This is the beginning of the pre-open market session before regular trading starts.- During this time, traders can place, modify, or cancel orders.- The exchange collects orders to determine the opening price. PreOpenEnd 1 - This marks the end of the pre-open session.- The exchange processes all collected orders and calculates the opening market price.- Regular trading is about to begin after this phase. NormalStart 2 - This is the start of the normal trading session.- Buy and sell orders are matched continuously in real time.- Most market trading activity happens during this period. NormalEnd 4 - This indicates the end of the regular trading session.- New trades under normal market rules stop after this point.- The market then moves to the next session, such as post-closing. PostClosingStart 8 - This is the beginning of the post-closing session after normal trading ends.- Certain order types may still be accepted depending on exchange rules.- It helps complete settlement-related or closing-price activities. PostClosingEnd 16 - This marks the end of the post-closing session.- All special post-market activities are completed.- The market prepares to move into the closed state. Closed 32 - The market is completely closed for trading.- No new buy or sell transactions can be executed.- This usually occurs after market hours, weekends, or holidays. None 256 - This means no market session status is currently assigned or available.- It may be used as a default or placeholder value in the system.- Applications often show this when session information is unavailable.

docs.title: 6. Exchange Market Type
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Normal 1 - Regular trading process jahan exchange ke standard rules follow hote hain.- Sabhi orders normal market timings mein execute kiye jaate hain.- Daily buying aur selling ke liye sabse commonly used category hai. OddLot 2 - Jab quantity standard trading lot se kam ya alag hoti hai tab use kiya jaata hai.- Aise orders special handling ke saath process hote hain.- Small quantity transactions ke liye suitable hai. RetailDebt 3 - Retail investors ke liye debt instruments (Bonds, NCDs, etc.) ki trading.- Ismein fixed-income securities ko buy ya sell kiya ja sakta hai.- Regular equity trading se alag debt market transactions ke liye use hota hai. Auction 4 - Auction session mein pending ya unsettled positions ko resolve karne ke liye use hota hai.- Exchange required securities ki buying ya selling auction process se karwata hai.- Settlement obligations complete karne mein madad karta hai. CallAuction1 5 - Pre-defined auction window jahan orders collect kiye jaate hain.- Matching ek fixed time par hoti hai, continuously nahi.- Price discovery aur fair order execution ke liye use kiya jaata hai. CallAuction2 6 - Call Auction ka doosra phase ya session.- Collected orders ko match karke final execution kiya jaata hai.- Market mein transparency aur efficient price determination ensure karta hai.

docs.title: 7. CallAuction Type
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description NonCallAuction 0 - Regular market segment jahan trading continuous basis par hoti hai.- Orders aate hi matching rules ke according execute hote hain.- Call Auction mechanism is segment mein apply nahi hota. PreOpen 1 - Market open hone se pehle orders collect aur match kiye jaate hain.- Is session ka purpose opening price determine karna hota hai.- Trading start hone se pehle fair price discovery ensure karta hai. IPOPreOpen 2 - Naye IPO listed stock ke liye special pre-open session.- Orders collect karke initial listing price discover ki jaati hai.- Listing day par smooth aur transparent market opening mein madad karta hai. RelistPreOpen 3 - Relisted security ke liye market open hone se pehle ka session.- Orders collect karke opening price determine ki jaati hai.- Relisting ke baad fair trading start karne mein help karta hai. Illiquid 4 - Kam trading volume aur low market activity wali securities.- Inmein buyers aur sellers ki availability limited ho sakti hai.- Price movements comparatively zyada volatile ho sakte hain. SME 5 - Small and Medium Enterprises ki listed securities ka segment.- Yeh platform growing businesses ko capital raise karne ka mauka deta hai.- SME companies ke shares ki trading ke liye use kiya jaata hai. SCAS 6 - Special Call Auction Session ke under aane wali securities.- Orders ek fixed auction process ke through collect aur match kiye jaate hain.- Price discovery aur controlled trading environment provide karta hai.

docs.title: 8. BookType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description None 0 - No special order condition is applied to the trade.- The order follows the default market trading process.- Used for standard buy and sell transactions. Regular 1 - Order is placed in the normal trading market segment.- It follows standard exchange rules and timings.- Most day-to-day trading activities use this category. SpecialTerms 2 - Order is subject to specific exchange-defined conditions.- Execution may follow additional settlement or trading rules.- Used when standard trading terms do not apply. StopLoss 3 - Order is triggered only when a specified price is reached.- Helps limit potential losses in volatile markets.- Commonly used for risk management and capital protection. Negotiated 4 - Trade is executed based on terms agreed between parties.- Price and quantity are decided before execution.- Typically used for special or large-value transactions. OddLot 5 - Order quantity is smaller than the standard market lot size.- It allows trading of non-standard share quantities.- Commonly used for small holdings or partial transactions. Spot 6 - Trade settlement is completed on the same day or immediately.- Ownership transfer happens faster than regular settlement.- Used when quick settlement is required. Auction 7 - Order participates in an exchange auction session.- Matching occurs through an auction-based price discovery process.- Used for special market events and settlement requirements. CallAuction1 11 - Orders are collected during the first call auction session.- Execution happens at a single price after order collection.- Helps determine a fair market price before trading. CallAuction2 12 - Orders are collected during the second call auction session.- Matching is performed at a calculated auction price.- Provides additional price discovery and orderly execution.

docs.title: 9. OptionType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description CA 1 - CA — Corporate Action- Provides information about company actions such as dividends, stock splits, bonus issues, and mergers.- Helps track changes that can affect a stock's value and shareholder holdings. PA 2 - PA — Price Action- Provides data about how a stock's price moves over time.- Includes trends, price changes, highs, lows, and market movement patterns. CE 3 - CE — Corporate Event- Provides details about important company-related events.- Includes earnings announcements, board meetings, annual meetings, and disclosures. PE 4 - PE — Price Event- Provides alerts or records of significant price-related movements.- Includes sharp price increases, decreases, or predefined price threshold triggers. None 5 - No specific event type is selected.- Data will not be filtered by any event category.- Use this option when you want the default or unfiltered market data.

docs.title: 10. PublishFormat
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Binary 1 - Returns market data in a compact binary format for faster processing and lower bandwidth usage.- Optimized for high-performance applications that require maximum speed and efficiency.- Best suited for systems that can parse and decode binary data formats. JSON 2 - Returns market data in a human-readable JSON format.- Easy to integrate, debug, and use across most programming languages and applications.- Best suited for development, testing, and standard API integrations.

docs.title: 11. BroadCastMode
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Full 1 - Returns the complete set of available market data for the requested instrument or event.- Includes all relevant fields and details without any data reduction.- Best suited when comprehensive information is required for analysis or reporting. Partial 2 - Returns only a subset of the available market data.- Includes essential fields to reduce response size and improve performance.- Best suited when only key information is needed for faster processing.

docs.title: 12. Socket Event
docs.text: Enum Name Description joined - WebSocket Joined- Sent when a client successfully connects and joins the WebSocket channel.- Confirms that the real-time data stream is active and ready. error - Error Event- Indicates a failure during WebSocket connection or request processing.- Includes invalid request, authentication failure, or system error. warning - Warning Message- Non-critical advisory message from the server.- Example: rate limit approaching or deprecated API usage detected. success - Success Response- Confirms that a client request was processed successfully.- Example: subscription to an instrument acknowledged.

docs.title: Socket Streaming
docs.text:
Socket Streaming

Socket Streaming creates a live connection between your application and the Market Data server. Once connected, market updates are automatically pushed in real time — no repeated requests needed.

Real-time updates Low latency No repeated calls WebSocket based Live price & depth Efficient bandwidth

docs.title: How Socket Streaming Works
docs.text:
Connect → Subscribe → Receive Updates → Unsubscribe → Disconnect 1. Connect

Establish a WebSocket connection with the Market Data server using your authentication token.

2. Subscribe

Subscribe to instruments using Exchange Segment and Exchange Instrument ID. Server starts tracking them.

3. Receive Updates

Server automatically pushes data whenever market changes occur. No additional requests needed.

4. Unsubscribe

Stop receiving updates for specific instruments at any time without closing the connection.

5. Disconnect

Close the WebSocket connection when streaming is no longer required.

docs.title: Socket Events
docs.text: Event Description joined - Socket connection established successfully.- Fired when the client connects to the WebSocket server. success - A request or operation completed successfully.- Returned after a valid subscribe or unsubscribe action. warning - A non-critical issue that may require attention.- Does not stop the connection but should be noted. error - An operation failed or could not be completed.- Check the error message for details and retry if needed. trade - Sent when a trade is executed in the market.- Contains trade price, quantity, and time details. order - Sent when an order-related update is available.- Includes status changes like filled, partial fill, or cancelled. position - Sent when there is a change in positions or holdings.- Helps track live portfolio changes in real time. logout - User has been disconnected from the socket session.- Reconnection may be required after this event. tradeConversion - Sent when a position is converted from one product type to another.- Example: MIS to NRML or CNC conversion. getOrder - Returns details of existing orders.- Use to fetch current order status and information. getOrderRejection - Returns information about rejected orders.- Includes the rejection reason for debugging and user notification.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
To receive streaming Market Data events, you must use the Socket.IO library. For more information, visit: https://socket.io/.

Real-Time Streaming Flow

Once the connection is established, real-time streaming data can be obtained by listening to the socket on the relevant market data ports. The streaming data will be received on these ports, and upon receiving the data, you are free to process it as required.

Below are the steps to follow to correctly implement the real-time streaming flow:

  1. Establish the socket connection
  2. Listen to real-time streaming events

docs.title: Establishment of Socket Connection
docs.text:
You can connect to the server by sending the userID, token, source, and broadcastMode as query parameters. The token is available only after a successful RESTful login request, as described in the RESTful section of the documentation.

import socketio # Base URL of the ApiMarketdata API server url = "https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000" # Required credentials userID = "" token = "" broadcastMode = "Full" # "Partial" publishFormat = "JSON" socketio_path = "/apibinarymarketdata/socketio" logger = False # True # Create Socket.IO client sio = socketio.Client() connectionString = f"{url}?token={token}&userID={userID}&publishFormat={publishFormat}&broadcastMode={broadcastMode}" @sio.on("connect") def connect(): print("Connection Established") @sio.on("disconnect") def disconnect(): print("Disconnected") @sio.on("joined") def joined(data): print("Socket Joined", data) @sio.on("error") def error(data): print("Error", data) 📋 Copy

docs.title: Listening to Real-Time Streaming
docs.text: Once the socket connection is successfully established, you can listen to real-time streaming data by subscribing to the attached market data ports. The complete market data will be received as a string.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
The user needs to connect to the server via a socket (i.e., WebSocket). It is important to set the path parameter value as /socket.io during the connection. The token will only be available after a successful login, so make sure you log in first before connecting to the server via socket.

Here, the URL is the REST API address used to connect to the interactive server (e.g., www.test.example.com). Once connected to the server, you can listen to the following events: SocketEvents. An example of a connect event is given below

@sio.on("connect") def connect(): print("Connection Established") 📋 Copy

docs.title: Joined
docs.text:
If a successful connection is established with the server, this event will be raised to indicate that the user has been connected.

@sio.on("joined") def on_joined(data): print("Socket Joined", data) 📋 Copy

docs.title: Error
docs.text:
In case of any error with the server, this event will be raised along with the cause of the error. For example, if you send an incorrect token while connecting, the server will raise this event and disconnect your socket connection.

@sio.on("error") def on_error(data): print("Error", data) 📋 Copy

docs.title: Disconnect
docs.text:
In case a socket disconnection occurs with the server, this event will be raised to indicate the disconnection.

@sio.on("disconnect") def on_disconnect(): print("Disconnected") 📋 Copy

docs.title: Subscribe to Socket
docs.text:
This API request is used to subscribe to market data over a WebSocket connection for specified exchange instruments and message codes provided in the request. Upon successful subscription, the user receives an acknowledgment response containing the latest quote data along with the remaining subscription count, which is AppKey-specific and configurable via the API dashboard. Once subscribed, real-time market data for the specified instrument(s) will be continuously streamed on the market data WebSocket.

URL

PUT https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/instruments/subscription 📋 Copy

Request Body Parameters

Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description instruments Array Y Array of instrument objects exchangeSegment ExchangeSegment Y ExchangeSegment exchangeInstrumentID ExchangeInstrumentID Y Exchange Scrip code or Symbol Token is unique identifier MessageCode Integer Y It is system generated message code

Request Body JSON

{ "instruments": [ { "exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 22 } ], "xtsMessageCode": 1582 } 📋 Copy

Response Body JSON

{ "type": "success", "code": "s-session-0001", "description": "Instrument subscribed successfully!", "result": { "mdp": 1501, "quotesList": [ { "exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 22 } ], "listQuotes": [ "{\"MessageCode\":1501,\"ExchangeSegment\":1,\"ExchangeInstrumentID\":\"22\",\"LastTradedPrice\":1723,\"LastTradedQunatity\":15,\"TotalBuyQuantity\":18446,\"TotalSellQuantity\":25283,\"TotalTradedQuantity\":189238,\"Average...\"}" ], "Remaining_Subscription_Count": 48 } } 📋 Copy

docs.title: Unsubscribe to Socket
docs.text:
This API request is used to unsubscribe from market data streaming for instruments that are already subscribed. Upon successful unsubscription, the server sends an acknowledgment confirming the unsubscription, stops sending market data for the specified instrument(s) on the WebSocket, and releases the corresponding subscription count, making it available for future subscriptions.

URL
