docs.title: Market Depth
docs.text:
Market Depth

Market Depth provides real-time visibility into the full order book — all pending buy and sell orders at every price level. It shows market liquidity, supply and demand, and potential price pressure far beyond the last traded price.

Trading Terminals Liquidity Analysis Support & Resistance Algorithmic Trading Order Flow Analysis

docs.title: What is Market Depth?
docs.text:
The order book is a real-time list of every pending buy and sell order for an instrument. Market Depth shows you the top 5 levels on each side — price, quantity waiting at that price, and how many individual orders are queued there.

Bids (Buy Orders)

Pending orders from buyers. Listed from highest to lowest price. The top bid is the highest a buyer will pay right now.

Buy Side Spread

The gap between the best ask and the best bid. A smaller spread means more buyers and sellers are actively trading.

Center Gap Asks (Sell Orders)

Pending orders from sellers. Listed from lowest to highest price. The top ask is the minimum price a seller will accept.

Sell Side

docs.title: API Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /apimarketdata/instruments/quotes xtsMessageCode: 1502

Market Depth data uses the same quotes endpoint as touchline data — pass xtsMessageCode: 1502 to receive the 5-level order book instead of just LTP and OHLC.

docs.title: Request and Response
Response Fields
docs.text: Bids[ ] — Buy Side FieldDescription PriceBid price at this level SizeTotal quantity waiting at this price TotalOrdersNumber of individual orders at this price Asks[ ] — Sell Side FieldDescription PriceAsk price at this level SizeTotal quantity available at this price TotalOrdersNumber of individual sellers at this price

docs.title: Bid, Ask, and Spread
docs.text: Bid Price ₹2965.40 The highest price buyers currently want to pay. If you sell at market, you get this price. Best Buy Order Spread Ask − Bid = ₹0.20 Tighter spread = more liquid. Wider spread = fewer active traders, higher cost to trade. Liquidity Signal Ask Price ₹2965.60 The lowest price sellers are willing to accept. If you buy at market, you pay this price. Best Sell Order

docs.title: Reading Market Liquidity
docs.text:
The depth and size of the order book tells you how easily you can execute a large order without moving the market price.

High Liquidity Large quantities on both bid and ask sides. Tight spread. Orders fill quickly at the expected price. Ideal for large orders. Tight spread (₹0.05 – ₹0.20) High total bid/ask quantity Many orders per level Low Liquidity Thin order book with small quantities. Wide spread. Large orders can move the price significantly. Risky for big trades. Wide spread (₹1 – ₹5+) Low total bid/ask quantity Few orders per level

docs.title: Identifying Support and Resistance
docs.text:
Large concentrations of orders at specific price levels can act as support (large buy orders) or resistance (large sell orders).

Support Level A price where a significant number of buy orders are stacked. The market often bounces back up when it reaches this level because buyers absorb selling pressure. 2965.30 — 1,800 qty 2965.20 — 850 qty 2965.00 — 12,000 qty ← Support Resistance Level A price where a significant number of sell orders are stacked. The market often struggles to break above this level because sellers keep absorbing buying pressure. 2970.00 — 15,000 qty ← Resistance 2969.50 — 600 qty 2969.00 — 900 qty

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text: 1 Client Application Sends instrument token with xtsMessageCode 1502 2 Market Depth API Routes to the exchange order book data feed 3 Exchange Order Book Real-time snapshot of top 5 bid and ask levels 4 Depth Response Bids[ ] and Asks[ ] arrays — price, size, order count 5 Trading Terminal Renders order book, spread, and liquidity visualization

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Combine with Quote Data

Use market depth alongside the last traded price and OHLC to get the complete market picture before placing an order.

Check Liquidity Before Large Orders

Before placing a large order, verify there is enough quantity at the top levels. Thin books can cause significant slippage.

Use WebSocket for Live Updates

Subscribe to event code 1502 via WebSocket instead of polling. Order books update many times per second.

Watch for Order Book Imbalance

A large imbalance in total bid vs ask quantity often signals short-term price direction — more bids = buy pressure, more asks = sell pressure.

docs.title: Common Errors
docs.text: 404 Instrument Not Found The instrument token does not exist in the specified exchange segment. 401 Unauthorized Market data token is missing, expired, or invalid. 429 Rate Limit Exceeded Too many depth requests. Use WebSocket streaming for continuous updates.

docs.title: OHLC Data
docs.text:
OHLC Data

The OHLC API provides historical candlestick price data for any tradable instrument — the foundation of every charting system, technical indicator, and backtesting engine. Each candle encodes four prices (Open, High, Low, Close) over a specific time interval.

Candlestick Charts Technical Indicators Backtesting Market Trend Analysis Price Performance

docs.title: What is OHLC?
docs.text:
OHLC stands for Open, High, Low, Close. Each value describes a different price point within a fixed time window — whether that window is 1 minute or 1 day.

O Open The first traded price when the candle interval began. For a daily candle this is the market open price. ₹2940.00 H High The maximum price reached during the entire candle interval. Represents the top of the upper wick. ₹2975.25 L Low The minimum price reached during the entire candle interval. Represents the bottom of the lower wick. ₹2935.80 C Close The last traded price when the candle interval ended. This is the most important price for most indicators. ₹2965.50

docs.title: Candlestick Structure
docs.text: High₹2975.25 Close₹2965.50 Bullish Close > Open Open₹2940.00 Low₹2935.80 Wick (Shadow) Thin vertical lines showing the full High-to-Low range for the interval Green Body (Bullish) Close is higher than Open — price moved up during this interval Red Body (Bearish) Close is lower than Open — price moved down during this interval

docs.title: API Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /apimarketdata/instruments/ohlc

Returns historical OHLC candle data for a specific instrument. Pass the exchange segment, instrument ID, time range, and compression interval in the request body.

docs.title: Request and Response
Request Parameters
docs.text: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription exchangeSegmentIntegerYesExchange segment code (1=NSECM, 2=NSEFO, etc.) exchangeInstrumentIDIntegerYesUnique instrument token from the master file startTimeStringYesStart of the historical range — format: Mmm DD YYYY HHMMSS endTimeStringYesEnd of the historical range — same format as startTime compressionValueIntegerYesCandle interval in minutes (see table below)

docs.title: Supported Intervals (compressionValue)
docs.text: 1 1 Minute Intraday scalping, HFT signals 5 5 Minutes Intraday momentum strategies 15 15 Minutes Short-term trend following 30 30 Minutes Intraday support and resistance 60 1 Hour Swing trading, multi-day trends 1440 1 Day Long-term analysis, EOD charts

docs.title: Response Format — Parsed
docs.text:
Split the pipe-separated string on || to get candles, then split each candle on | to get the 7 fields:

0 Timestamp 1718342400 Unix epoch seconds — convert to datetime 1 Open 2940.00 First traded price in interval 2 High 2975.25 Highest price in interval 3 Low 2935.80 Lowest price in interval 4 Close 2965.50 Last traded price in interval 5 Volume 1254789 Total quantity traded 6 Open Interest 0 Outstanding contracts (F&O only)

docs.title: Intraday Candle OHLC
docs.text:
The XTS Front-end API provides intraday archived OHLC (candlestick) data from the date of access for Equity segments of NSECM and BSECM. For FO segments, OHLC data is available only for currently traded contracts, and expired contracts are not supported.

The response is delivered in candle format, including timestamp (epoch time since 1970), Open, High, Low, Close, Volume, and Open Interest (OI). The minimum supported interval is 60 seconds (1 minute), with additional supported intervals for the GET OHLC request detailed in the table below.

Request Body Parameters

docs.title: Technical Analysis with OHLC
docs.text:
Every major technical indicator is derived from OHLC values. Here are the most commonly computed using this data:

Trend Indicators Moving Average (MA) Exponential MA (EMA) MACD SuperTrend Parabolic SAR Momentum Indicators RSI Stochastic Oscillator CCI Williams %R MFI Volatility Indicators Bollinger Bands ATR Keltner Channel Donchian Channel Volume & Price VWAP OBV Support Levels Resistance Levels Pivot Points

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text: 1 Client Application Sends instrument token, time range, and compression interval 2 OHLC API Validates request parameters and routes to historical data store 3 Historical Market Data Fetches tick data, aggregates into OHLC candles by interval 4 OHLC Response Pipe-delimited candle data returned in chronological order 5 Charts and Analytics Parse, render, and compute indicators on the candle array

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Match Interval to Strategy

Use 1-min candles for intraday scalping, 1-day candles for swing trading. Fetching daily candles for a 1-min strategy wastes data resolution.

Request Only What You Need

Narrow the date range to the minimum required. Fetching years of 1-min data is slow and expensive — paginate if you need large historical ranges.

Cache Historical Data

Past candles never change. Once fetched, store them locally and only request the most recent candles on subsequent calls.

Use WebSocket for Live Candles

For the current (in-progress) candle, use WebSocket message code 1505 instead of polling the OHLC endpoint every second.

docs.title: What is Market Data?
docs.text:
Market data is information generated by exchanges during trading hours. It helps you track live prices, analyze trends, and make informed trading decisions.

RELIANCE • NSE ₹2,850.00 +25.50 (0.90%) ↗ Open2,820.00 High2,870.00 Low2,810.00 Prev. Close2,824.50 Volume1,200,000

docs.title: Types of Market Data
docs.text:
Live Data

Real-time data received instantly from exchanges.

Example: LTP, Bid, Ask, Volume Delayed Data

Data received with a short delay (e.g., 15 minutes).

Example: 15-min Delayed Data Historical Data

Previously recorded data for past dates.

Example: Daily, Weekly, Monthly

Real-time Quotes

Get the latest price, change, volume and other market details in real-time.

Historical Data

Access historical data for analysis, backtesting and trend identification.

Retrieve Open, High, Low, Close data for any time interval.

Market Depth

View real-time buy and sell orders in the market depth (order book).

Instrument Info

Get details about instruments like lot size, tick size, expiry, and trading symbol.

Live & Historical

docs.title: Instruments
docs.text:
Instruments

The Instruments API provides the master list of all tradable securities across supported exchanges — stocks, futures, options, currencies, indices, and commodities. It is the foundation for every other API in the platform.

Search securities by name or symbol Retrieve instrument tokens for market data subscriptions Get correct exchange and segment identifiers Validate lot size and tick size before placing orders Map trading symbols across Quotes, OHLC, and WebSocket APIs Build symbol search for your trading application

docs.title: What is an Instrument?
docs.text:
An instrument is any financial asset that can be traded in a market. Every security — whether it is a stock, derivative, or currency pair — is represented as an instrument in the RMoney API.

Reliance Industries TCS NIFTY 50 Bank Nifty Futures USDINR NIFTY 25000 CE

docs.title: Instrument Structure
docs.text:
Every instrument belongs to an exchange and segment. The full hierarchy from exchange down to trading symbol is:

Exchange Trading venue — NSE, BSE, MCX NSE Segment Asset class — Equity, F&O, Currency Equity (CM) Instrument The actual security Reliance Industries Ltd Trading Symbol Symbol used in API calls RELIANCE

docs.title: Instrument Types
docs.text: Equity Company shares listed on NSE or BSE cash market. RELIANCETCSINFYHDFCBANK NSE CM BSE CM Futures Contracts to buy or sell an asset at a specified future date and price. NIFTY JUL FUTBANKNIFTY JUL FUTRELIANCE FUT NSE FO MCX FO Options Contracts giving the right (not obligation) to buy or sell at a strike price. NIFTY 25000 CENIFTY 25000 PE Call (CE) Put (PE) Currency Foreign exchange instruments traded on the NSE Currency Derivatives segment. USDINREURINRGBPINR NSE CD Indices Market benchmarks representing a basket of securities. Not directly tradable — used for reference and derivatives. NIFTY 50BANK NIFTYSENSEX Reference only

docs.title: Understanding Key Fields
docs.text: ExchangeInstrumentID The unique numeric identifier for this instrument on the exchange. This is the token you pass to Quotes, OHLC, and WebSocket APIs. Example2885 Used in: Quotes API, OHLC API, WebSocket subscriptions ExchangeSegment Integer code identifying which exchange segment the instrument belongs to. Must match when placing orders or fetching data. 1 = NSECM2 = NSEFO3 = NSECD 11 = BSECM51 = MCXFO TradingSymbol The exchange-recognized symbol used when placing buy/sell orders. For derivatives, includes expiry and strike details. EquityRELIANCE FutureNIFTY25JULFUT OptionNIFTY2572025000CE LotSize Minimum tradeable quantity. For equity the lot size is 1. For derivatives, orders must be in multiples of the lot size or the exchange will reject them. NIFTY FUT75 units BANKNIFTY FUT35 units RELIANCE EQ1 unit TickSize The minimum price increment for a limit order. Prices that are not multiples of tick size are rejected by the exchange. 100.00 100.05 100.10 100.03 — invalid Series The instrument series defines the type of financial contract within an exchange segment. EQ FUTIDX FUTSTK OPTIDX OPTSTK

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
1 Search Before Trading

Search by company name to find the correct trading symbol and instrument ID before placing an order.

Search "Reliance" Get RELIANCE + token 2885 Place order with RELIANCE 2 Subscribe to Market Data

Get the instrument token and pass it to the Quotes or WebSocket API to receive live prices.

Fetch token = 2885 Subscribe via WebSocket Receive live LTP 3 Build a Symbol Directory

Download the full master file daily at market open. Cache it locally so your app can do instant symbol lookups without hitting the API on every search.

Download master on startup Parse into local index Search from cache

docs.title: Instruments API Workflow
docs.text: 1 Fetch Instruments Master Download the full list once per day at market start 2 Search Instrument Look up by name or symbol to get token and exchange 3 Get Instrument Token Extract ExchangeInstrumentID and ExchangeSegment 4 Fetch Quotes / Subscribe WebSocket Pass the token to get live market data 5 Place Order Use TradingSymbol + ExchangeSegment in the order payload

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Cache the Master File Locally

The master file contains thousands of instruments. Download once at startup and cache in memory — don't re-fetch on every symbol lookup.

Refresh Daily

The master file changes each day (new contracts, expired options). Re-download at market open (9:00 AM) to stay current.

Use Instrument Tokens, Not Names

Always use ExchangeInstrumentID for API calls. Symbol names can change; tokens are stable identifiers used by the exchange.

Verify Lot Size Before Orders

Check the lot size for every derivative before placement. An order quantity that is not a multiple of lot size will be rejected.

docs.text: 404 Instrument Not Found The instrument ID or symbol does not exist in the exchange segment. 400 Invalid Exchange The ExchangeSegment code is incorrect or not supported. 400 Invalid Symbol The TradingSymbol does not match any instrument in the segment. 410 Instrument Expired The contract (futures/options) has passed its expiry date.

docs.title: Master
docs.text:
Master

XTS provides an API call to fetch all tradable instruments as well as additional data in a single structure. This call can be made once per day, and the response can be persisted in local storage or a file based on your application design. You can then fetch instruments or symbols from this dataset throughout the day.

The structure of the response is as follows. The pipe (|) and line-separated values can be easily tokenized and bulk-loaded into your storage of choice.

docs.title: Instrument By Search String
docs.text:
Instrument By Search String

You can search for instruments by using the GET /search/instruments request. In the response, you will receive the instrument details based on the searchString provided in the request.

Endpoint

GET https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata//apimarketdata/search/instruments Copy Request Body Parameters Parameter NameTypeMandatoryDescription searchStringStringYSearch keyword to find matching instruments (e.g., RELIANCE) Response Body Parameters Parameter NameTypeDescription ExchangeSegmentExchangeSegment ↗Exchange segment in which the instrument is listed. ExchangeInstrumentIDExchangeInstrumentID 👁Exchange script code or Symbol Token is unique identifier. InstrumentTypeInstrumentType ↗Type of financial instrument. NameName 👁The official symbol or short name of the instrument as defined by the exchange. DisplayNameDisplayName 👁A user-friendly name of the instrument used for display purposes in applications. DescriptionDescription 👁A detailed description of the instrument, including company or contract details. SeriesSeries 👁The exchange-defined series under which the instrument is listed (e.g., EQ, BL, A). NameWithSeriesNameWithSeries 👁The instrument name appended with its series (e.g., ‘RELIANCE-EQ’). InstrumentIDInstrumentID 👁A unique system-generated identifier assigned to the instrument or trading system. PriceBandObjectThe permitted price range within which the instrument can trade during a session. HighHigh 👁The upper limit of the price band for the instrument. LowLow 👁The lower limit of the price band for the instrument. CreditRatingCreditRating 👁The credit rating assigned to the instrument, if applicable (typically for debt instruments). HighStringHighString 👁The upper price band is represented as a formatted string. LowStringLowString 👁The lower price band is represented as a formatted string. HighExecBandStringHighExecBandString 👁The upper execution price band displayed as a formatted string. LowExecBandStringLowExecBandString 👁The lower execution price band displayed as a formatted string. FreezeQtyFreezeQty 👁The maximum order quantity allowed per order for the instrument. TickSizeTickSize 👁The minimum price movement allowed for the instrument. LotSizeLotSize 👁The minimum tradable quantity for the instrument. UnderlyingInstrumentIdUnderlyingInstrumentId 👁The unique instrument identifier of the underlying asset for a derivative contract. UnderlyingIndexNameUnderlyingIndexName 👁The name of the underlying index on which the derivative contract is based. ContractExpirationStringContractExpirationString 👁The contract expiration date represented as a formatted string. RemainingExpiryDaysRemainingExpiryDays 👁The number of calendar days remaining until the contract expires. ExchangeSegmentExchangeSegment ↗Exchange segment in which the instrument is listed. ExchangeInstrumentIDExchangeInstrumentID 👁Exchange script code or Symbol Token is unique identifier. docs.text:
Constants

Constants are fixed values used throughout the API to represent predefined information such as exchange segments, market types, order statuses, and product types — keeping API communication standardized and reliable.

Standardized values Reduces errors Consistent API data Easy validation Better readability Reliable integration

Enums

Enums are fixed values used by the API to represent specific categories such as exchanges, instrument types, market types, and order statuses — keeping API communication consistent and error-free.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
WebSocket Connection

WebSocket Connection is the first step in real-time market data streaming. It creates a live link between your application and the Market Data server, allowing market updates to be delivered instantly.

Secure connection Token authentication Live streaming Auto-reconnect Low latency Continuous session

docs.title: How Connection Works
docs.text:
Login via REST → Initiate Connection → Authenticate → joined Event → Subscribe & Stream 1. Login via REST

Login through the REST API to receive a Market Data token and userID.

2. Initiate Connection

Client sends a connection request to the WebSocket server endpoint.

3. Authenticate

Server validates the token. If valid, the WebSocket connection is established.

4. joined Event

Server fires the joined event confirming the connection is active.

5. Subscribe & Stream

Client subscribes to instruments and live data starts streaming automatically.

docs.title: Connection Status Events
docs.text: Event Description joined - Connection established successfully.- Fired when the client connects and is authenticated by the server. success - Connection request processed successfully.- Returned after a valid connect or subscribe action completes. error - Connection could not be established or authentication failed.- Check the token validity and server URL before retrying. logout - Session ended and connection has been closed.- Reconnect and re-authenticate to resume streaming.

docs.title: Step 1 — Login via REST
docs.text: from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect client = XTSConnect( apiKey="your_api_key", secretKey="your_secret_key", source="WEBAPI", root="https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000" ) await client.marketdata_login() # client.token and client.userID are now set

docs.title: Step 2 — Connect Market Data WebSocket
docs.text: from xts_api_client.market_data_socket import MDSocket_io from xts_api_client.market_data_socket_client import MarketDataSocketClient class MyPriceFeed(MarketDataSocketClient): async def on_connect(self): print("Connected to market data feed!") async def on_event_last_traded_price_full(self, data): print(f"LTP: {data['TradingSymbol']} @ {data['LastTradedPrice']}") socket = MDSocket_io( token=client.token, userID=client.userID, root_url=client.root, marketdatasocketclient=MyPriceFeed() ) await socket.connect()

docs.title: Step 3 — Connect Interactive WebSocket
docs.text: from xts_api_client.interactive_socket import OrderSocket_io from xts_api_client.interactive_socket_client import InteractiveSocketClient class MyOrderFeed(InteractiveSocketClient): async def on_order(self, data): print(f"Order: {data['OrderStatus']} for {data['TradingSymbol']}") order_socket = OrderSocket_io( token=interactive_client.token, userID=interactive_client.userID, root_url=interactive_client.root, reconnection=True ) await order_socket.connect()

docs.title: Step 4 — Subscribe to Instruments
docs.text: instruments = [ { "exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 2885 }, # RELIANCE { "exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 22 } # NIFTY ] await client.send_subscription(Instruments=instruments, xtsMessageCode=1512)

docs.title: Step 5 — Unsubscribe and Disconnect
docs.text: await client.send_unsubscription(Instruments=instruments, xtsMessageCode=1512) await socket.disconnect() await client.marketdata_logout()

docs.title: Connection Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description token - Session token from the Login API.- Required to authenticate the WebSocket connection. userID - User ID returned from the Login API.- Identifies the user session on the server. root_url - Base URL of the Market Data server.- Example: https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 reconnection - Auto-reconnect on disconnect.- Set to True to automatically reconnect if the connection drops.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Real-time

Instant data on market change

Low Latency

Minimal delay in delivery

Continuous

Stays open throughout session

Fewer Calls

No repeated REST polling

Auto-Reconnect

Handles drops gracefully

!!! tip Always login via REST before connecting the WebSocket. The token from login is required to authenticate the socket connection.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
WebSocket Events

WebSocket Events are real-time notifications sent by the server to inform the client about connection status, orders, trades, positions, and other important market activities.

Connection events Order updates Trade notifications Position changes Error alerts Real-time push

docs.title: Connection & System Events
docs.text: Event Description joined - WebSocket connection established successfully.- The client is now connected and ready to receive data.- Usually the first event received after connecting. success - A request or operation completed successfully.- Confirms that the requested action was processed.- Commonly received after a successful subscription request. warning - A non-critical issue or notification.- The connection remains active and operational.- Used to alert the client about potential issues. error - An operation failed or could not be completed.- Usually includes an error message or reason.- May occur due to invalid requests or authentication failures. logout - User session has ended and connection is closed.- No further updates will be received until reconnection.- Re-authenticate to resume streaming.

docs.title: Trading Events
docs.text: Event Description order - An order-related update has occurred.- Sent when an order is placed, modified, cancelled, or status changes.- Helps track order activity in real time. trade - A trade has been executed.- Sent when a buy and sell order are matched.- Provides trade execution details like price, quantity, and time. position - A position-related update has occurred.- Sent when there is a change in open positions or holdings.- Helps users monitor their portfolio in real time. tradeConversion - A trade or position has been converted.- Example: Converting a position from MIS to CNC.- Sent after successful product type conversion. getOrder - Returns details of existing orders.- Used to retrieve order information through the socket connection.- Provides current order status and related data. getOrderRejection - An order has been rejected.- Includes the rejection reason from the system or exchange.- Helps users identify and resolve order issues.

docs.title: Market Data Events
docs.text: Override these methods in your MarketDataSocketClient subclass to receive data.

docs.title: Connection Events
docs.text: class MyFeed(MarketDataSocketClient): async def on_connect(self): print("Connected!") async def on_disconnect(self): print("Disconnected!") async def on_error(self, data): print("Error:", data)

docs.title: Price Events
docs.text:
Event 1512 — LTP Only

Lightweight LTP-only tick. Lowest bandwidth option.

on_event_last_traded_price_full Event 1501 — Touchline

LTP plus best bid/ask and volume.

on_event_touchline_full Event 1502 — Market Depth

Full 5-level order book.

on_event_market_depth_full Event 1505 — OHLC Candle

Live Open, High, Low, Close candle data.

on_event_candle_data_full Event 1510 — Open Interest

Total active futures/options contracts.

on_event_open_interest_full Event 1507 — Market Status

Exchange session state updates.

on_event_instrument_property_change_full

docs.title: Interactive (Order) Events
docs.text: class MyOrderHandler(InteractiveSocketClient): async def on_order(self, data): print(f"Order {data['AppOrderID']} → {data['OrderStatus']}") async def on_trade(self, data): print(f"Trade: {data['TradingSymbol']}  {data['TradedQuantity']} @ {data['TradedPrice']}") async def on_position(self, data): print(f"Position: {data['TradingSymbol']}  NetQty: {data['NetQty']}")

docs.title: Event Code Reference
docs.text:
Code Event Bandwidth 1512 LTP only Very low 1501 Touchline (LTP + bid/ask) Low 1502 Full depth (5 levels) Medium 1505 OHLC candle Medium 1510 Open interest Low 1507 Market status Very low

!!! tip Subscribe only to the event codes you actually need. Using 1502 (full depth) for hundreds of instruments simultaneously uses significantly more bandwidth than 1512 (LTP only).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
WebSocket Overview

WebSocket creates a live connection between your application and the RMoney server. Once connected, the server automatically sends real-time market updates whenever prices or market information change — no repeated requests needed.

Real-time streaming Persistent connection Low latency Full-duplex Reduced API calls High volume data

docs.title: Two WebSocket Channels
docs.text:
Market Data Socket

Live prices, bid/ask, depth, OHLC ticks

{root}/?token=...&publishFormat=JSON&broadcastMode=Full Interactive Socket

Order updates, trade confirmations, position changes

{root}/?token=...&userID=...&apiType=INTERACTIVE

docs.title: WebSocket Lifecycle
docs.text:
Connect → Authenticate → Subscribe → Stream Data → Disconnect 1. Connect

Client establishes a WebSocket connection with the RMoney server.

2. Authenticate

Validates the session using the token received from the Login API.

3. Subscribe

Register instruments or data streams with an event code to start receiving updates.

4. Stream Data

Server continuously pushes market updates whenever data changes.

5. Unsubscribe

Stop updates for selected instruments without closing the connection.

6. Disconnect

Close the WebSocket connection when streaming is no longer needed.

docs.title: Event Codes (Market Data)
docs.text: Code Data Type Description 1512 LTP Only Last Traded Price only — minimal data, maximum speed. 1501 Touchline LTP, Bid, Ask, Volume, Open Interest — full top-of-book data. 1502 Market Depth Full 5-level bid/ask order book depth. 1505 OHLC Candle Live Open, High, Low, Close candle data for a given interval. 1510 Open Interest Total open futures/options contracts for a derivative instrument. 1507 Market Status Exchange session state — Open, Closed, Pre-open, etc.

docs.title: WebSocket vs REST API
docs.text:
REST API
  • Request every time data is needed
  • Higher latency per request
  • More network overhead
  • Not suitable for real-time feeds
→ WebSocket
  • Data pushed automatically on change
  • Ultra-low latency
  • Minimal network overhead
  • Built for real-time applications

docs.title: When to Use What
docs.text: Use Case Recommended Live price feed for a dashboard WebSocket — Market Data Real-time order status updates WebSocket — Interactive Fetching historical candles REST — OHLC endpoint Placing / modifying / cancelling orders REST — Interactive API One-time instrument lookup REST — Instruments endpoint

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Live Market Quotes

Stream real-time bid/ask prices for any instrument.

Touchline Streaming

Receive LTP, open, high, low, close, and volume updates.

Market Depth

View best 5 buy/sell prices and quantities in real time.

Index Updates

Track NIFTY, SENSEX, BANKNIFTY live index values.

Trade Notifications

Get instant alerts when trades are executed in the market.

Order & Position

Real-time order status and position change tracking.

See Connection for setup details and Events for handling data.
